The Assistants API improvements include a 500-fold increase in file ingestion capacity, streaming support for real-time responses, and support for fine-tuned GPT-3.5 Turbo models. Additionally, OpenAI offers discounted usage for committed throughput on GPT-4 and a new Batch API for asynchronous workloads at reduced costs. These updates reflect OpenAI's ongoing commitment to enterprise-grade security, administrative flexibility, and scalable cost management for AI deployments.

item.title: OpenAI commits to Safety by Design principles to prevent AI misuse in child sexual abuse material, joining industry leaders in a collaborative effort [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has joined a coalition of leading tech companies, including Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft, to adopt Safety by Design principles aimed at preventing generative AI from being misused to create or spread child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and other harms against children. This initiative, led by the nonprofit Thorn and All Tech Is Human, focuses on embedding child safety measures throughout AI development, deployment, and maintenance. The commitment includes responsibly sourcing training data, detecting and removing CSAM and child sexual exploitation material (CSEM), reporting confirmed cases to authorities, and implementing ongoing safety testing and misuse prevention. OpenAI has also set age restrictions for ChatGPT and collaborates with organizations like the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children to enhance reporting and protection mechanisms. The company plans to provide annual progress updates as part of this collective effort to prioritize child safety in AI technologies.

item.title: OpenAI proposes Instruction Hierarchy to train GPT-3.5 to prioritize privileged system instructions over user inputs, improving robustness against prompt injection attacks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI researchers address vulnerabilities in large language models that allow prompt injections and jailbreaks by proposing an Instruction Hierarchy. This approach trains models to prioritize privileged system instructions above user-provided prompts, reducing the risk of malicious overrides. The method was applied to GPT-3.5, significantly enhancing its resistance to various attack types while maintaining its standard capabilities with minimal degradation.

item.title: OpenAI opens first Asian office in Tokyo and launches GPT-4 custom model optimized for Japanese language [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has established its first office in Asia, located in Tokyo, Japan, and introduced a GPT-4 custom model specifically optimized for the Japanese language. The model offers improved performance in translating and summarizing Japanese text, operates up to three times faster than its predecessor, and is cost-effective. Tadao Nagasaki has been appointed President of OpenAI Japan to lead local operations and market engagement. The new office aims to collaborate with the Japanese government, businesses, and research institutions to develop AI tools tailored to Japan's needs. Major Japanese companies like Daikin, Rakuten, and TOYOTA Connected are already using ChatGPT Enterprise for business automation and data analysis, while local governments such as Yokosuka City report productivity gains from ChatGPT adoption. OpenAI plans to release the custom Japanese model more broadly via API in the coming months.

item.title: Klarna's AI assistant handles tasks equivalent to 700 full-time agents, improving customer service and driving $40 million profit in 2024 [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Klarna has deployed an AI assistant powered by OpenAI that manages customer service tasks across 23 markets and 35 languages, performing the work of 700 full-time agents and achieving customer satisfaction comparable to human agents. The assistant has handled 2.3 million conversations in its first month, reducing average resolution time from 11 minutes to under 2 minutes and cutting repeat inquiries by 25%. Beyond customer service, Klarna integrates AI throughout its organization, with 90% of employees using ChatGPT Enterprise tools daily to enhance productivity across departments such as Communications, Marketing, and Legal. The company expects the AI deployment to contribute approximately $40 million in profit improvement in 2024, while emphasizing the broader societal impact and the need for careful stewardship of AI technologies.

item.title: OpenAI updates fine-tuning API with new control features and expands Custom Models program with assisted fine-tuning collaboration [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has enhanced its fine-tuning API to give developers more control over training processes, including epoch-based checkpoints, a comparative playground for model evaluation, third-party integrations, and improved dashboard features. The company also expanded its Custom Models program by introducing assisted fine-tuning, a collaborative service with OpenAI researchers to optimize models using advanced techniques beyond the API. The fine-tuning API, launched for GPT-3.5 in August 2023, has been used by thousands of organizations to tailor models for specific tasks such as personalized job recommendations and code generation. Assisted fine-tuning supports organizations needing help with data pipelines, evaluation systems, and parameter tuning to maximize model performance. OpenAI is winding down the fine-tuning platform for new users but will maintain support for existing fine-tuned models until their base models are deprecated.

item.title: Harvey partners with OpenAI to develop a custom-trained case law AI model for legal professionals, enhancing document drafting and complex litigation research [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Harvey, a generative AI platform for law, tax, and finance professionals, has collaborated with OpenAI to create a custom-trained AI model focused on U.S. case law. This model aims to assist legal professionals by providing detailed, accurate answers with source citations, improving tasks such as drafting documents and analyzing complex litigation scenarios. The partnership involved integrating extensive legal data, including 10 billion tokens of case law, to build a model that surpasses general-purpose AI in legal reasoning and knowledge. Testing with major law firms showed a strong preference for Harvey's model over GPT-4, particularly due to its thoroughness and reduced hallucinations. Harvey plans to expand the model's applications to drafting briefs and understanding jurisdictional differences in case law.

item.title: OpenAI launches instant ChatGPT access without account registration, rolling out gradually to expand AI accessibility [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a new feature allowing users to start using ChatGPT immediately without signing up for an account, aiming to make AI tools more broadly accessible. This change applies globally and is being rolled out gradually to anyone curious about AI capabilities. Users can opt out of data sharing used to improve models, and additional content safeguards have been implemented for this experience. While account creation offers benefits like chat history saving and voice features, this update lowers barriers for first-time users to explore AI.

item.title: Oscar Health integrates OpenAI's GPT models to automate clinical documentation and claims processing, reducing costs and improving patient care efficiency [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Oscar Health is using OpenAI's language models to automate and speed up healthcare processes such as clinical documentation and claims handling, cutting documentation time by nearly 40% and claims escalation resolution by 50%. The company has also developed AI tools to analyze complex medical records, helping clinicians find relevant patient information faster and personalize care for patients with acute health conditions. Oscar emphasizes responsible AI use and HIPAA compliance through its partnership with OpenAI, aiming to improve healthcare equity and operational productivity.

item.title: OpenAI previews Voice Engine for custom synthetic voices using 15-second audio samples, exploring applications and safety challenges [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI shared early insights from a small-scale preview of Voice Engine, a model that generates natural-sounding synthetic voices from a single 15-second audio sample. The technology powers preset voices in OpenAI's text-to-speech API and ChatGPT Voice, and the company is cautiously evaluating broader deployment due to potential misuse risks. The preview involved trusted partners developing applications such as personalized reading assistance, multilingual content translation preserving native accents, support for non-verbal individuals, and clinical voice restoration. OpenAI is using these trials to inform safeguards and responsible deployment strategies while engaging in dialogue about the societal implications of synthetic voice technology.

item.title: Zelma uses GPT-4 to make US K-12 education data accessible and understandable for parents, educators, and policymakers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Zelma, powered by GPT-4, consolidates and cleans standardized test data from US students in grades 3-8 to provide accessible insights on English language arts and math performance. Developed by Dr. Emily Oster's team at Brown University and Novy using OpenAI's API, Zelma offers a conversational platform that suggests questions, displays SQL logic, and provides context to help users interpret education data effectively. The platform enables users to generate data visualizations quickly, such as identifying top-performing school districts or tracking achievement disparities over time, supporting informed decision-making by school boards, parents, and policymakers. Zelma aims to democratize education data that was previously scattered and underutilized, facilitating clearer discussions about student outcomes and educational equity.

item.title: OpenAI shares early feedback from artists using Sora to enhance creative workflows and explore new artistic possibilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduced Sora last month and has since collaborated with visual artists, designers, and filmmakers to understand how the tool can support creative processes. Early users report that Sora enables the realization of surreal and previously impossible ideas, expanding artistic expression beyond traditional constraints. Artists and creative directors from various disciplines have integrated Sora into their workflows, highlighting its ability to rapidly conceptualize high-quality visuals and prototype innovative concepts without typical technical or budgetary limitations. They emphasize Sora's potential to transform storytelling and artistic experimentation by removing conventional barriers and enabling new forms of creativity.

item.title: JetBrains integrates OpenAI API into its IDEs, launching its fastest-growing AI Assistant product to boost developer productivity [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: JetBrains has incorporated OpenAI's API into its AI Assistant product, embedded within its popular Integrated Development Environments (IDEs), to enhance developer productivity by automating routine coding tasks and providing intelligent code suggestions. This integration has led to the AI Assistant becoming the company's fastest-growing product, with a majority of developers reporting increased productivity and more time for engaging work. The AI Assistant offers features such as natural language prompts for code generation, automated documentation, error explanation, and code refactoring, all accessible directly within the IDE to reduce workflow disruptions. JetBrains selected OpenAI for its advanced reasoning capabilities, technical support, and superior performance metrics, and is continuing to develop new AI-driven features like project structure generation and terminal workflow automation to further accelerate software development.

item.title: Superhuman integrates OpenAI's API to launch AI-powered email features that double inbox processing and writing speed [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Superhuman has partnered with OpenAI to enhance email management by integrating AI features such as AI-generated email writing, rewriting in users' voices, auto summarization, and instant replies. These tools aim to reduce the time professionals spend on email, which currently totals around three hours daily for about one billion users worldwide. The integration leverages OpenAI's API to provide privacy-compliant, high-performance AI models that have led to over 85% user opt-in and increased engagement, with users writing emails twice as fast and processing inboxes twice as quickly. Superhuman envisions future AI agents that can automatically filter, triage, and respond to emails, further transforming the email experience.

item.title: Salesforce integrates OpenAI's enterprise-ready large language models to enhance Einstein 1 Platform with generative AI across sales, service, marketing, and commerce [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Salesforce has partnered with OpenAI to incorporate its enterprise-ready large language models into the Einstein 1 Platform, enabling generative AI capabilities across multiple customer applications including sales, service, marketing, and commerce. This integration aims to improve productivity by automating routine tasks and personalizing customer interactions while maintaining strong data privacy and security standards. The collaboration includes the introduction of the Einstein Trust Layer, a secure AI architecture designed to ensure data privacy and compliance with enterprise security requirements such as SOC-2. Salesforce offers no code, low code, and pro code tools for customers and developers to build tailored AI applications, enhancing workflows like sales account summaries and service chat responses. The partnership reflects Salesforce's focus on trust and safety as key priorities in deploying generative AI for business use cases.

item.title: Holiday Extras rolls out ChatGPT Enterprise across all teams, boosting productivity by 500 hours weekly through improved multilingual content, data fluency, and customer support [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Holiday Extras, a European travel extras provider, implemented ChatGPT Enterprise across its entire workforce, resulting in a productivity increase equivalent to 500 hours saved each week. The AI tool has enhanced various functions including marketing content localization, data analysis for non-technical staff, engineering productivity, UI/UX design rigor, and customer support efficiency. The company reported that 95% of employees use ChatGPT weekly, with 92% saving over two hours per week. ChatGPT has accelerated code debugging by 75% and enabled handling 30% of customer inquiries via AI bots, contributing to reduced support costs and improved customer satisfaction scores from 60% to 70%. Holiday Extras views this AI adoption as key to maintaining its innovation leadership in the travel-tech sector.

item.title: Healthify partners with OpenAI to enhance AI-driven health coaching for sustainable weight loss across 40 million users [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Healthify, India's largest health platform with over 40 million users, has partnered with OpenAI to improve its AI-powered health coaching and tracking tools aimed at promoting sustainable weight loss and reversing metabolic disease. The collaboration leverages OpenAI's GPT-4 Vision and embeddings to enhance food recognition accuracy and scale personalized coaching more efficiently. Previously, Healthify developed AI features like Ria, a virtual nutritionist, and Snap, a photo-based calorie counting tool, but faced challenges with accuracy and scaling across regions. Integrating OpenAI's models allowed Healthify to surpass prior performance, simplify integration, and fine-tune AI capabilities, enabling coaches to manage more clients and improve user engagement and health outcomes.

item.title: OpenAI partners with Le Monde and Prisa Media to integrate French and Spanish news content into ChatGPT [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has formed partnerships with international news organizations Le Monde and Prisa Media to incorporate their French and Spanish news content into ChatGPT, enhancing the platform's multilingual news offerings. These collaborations will allow ChatGPT users to access high-quality, authoritative news summaries with attribution and links to original articles from these publishers. Le Monde, France's leading news outlet with over 600,000 subscribers, and Prisa Media, a major Hispanic media group with a reach of more than 7 million daily unique users, aim to expand their audience through this integration. The partnerships also contribute to training OpenAI's models and reflect a strategic effort to support journalism by combining AI technology with credible news sources.

item.title: OpenAI completes governance review, confirms Sam Altman and Greg Brockman to continue leading, adds three new board members [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has completed a comprehensive review conducted by WilmerHale into the events surrounding the November 2023 removal of Sam Altman and Greg Brockman from its board and Altman's termination as CEO. Following the review, the board expressed full confidence in Altman and Brockman's leadership, with Altman rejoining the board as CEO. The organization also announced the appointment of three new board members with extensive leadership experience and introduced enhancements to its governance structure, including new corporate guidelines, a strengthened conflict of interest policy, a whistleblower hotline, and additional board committees focused on mission and strategy. The review involved over 30,000 documents and dozens of interviews with current and former board members, executives, and advisors. It found a breakdown in trust between the prior board and Altman that led to the November 17 actions but concluded these decisions were not related to concerns about product safety, development pace, finances, or communications. The expanded board aims to oversee OpenAI's growth and ensure its mission to benefit humanity through artificial general intelligence is pursued responsibly.

item.title: OpenAI adds Dr. Sue Desmond-Hellmann, Nicole Seligman, and Fidji Simo to board; Sam Altman rejoins [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI announced the addition of Dr. Sue Desmond-Hellmann, Nicole Seligman, and Fidji Simo to its board of directors, with CEO Sam Altman rejoining the board. These new members bring experience from global organizations in technology, nonprofit, and corporate governance sectors. They will collaborate with existing board members to oversee OpenAI's growth and mission to ensure artificial general intelligence benefits all humanity. Dr. Desmond-Hellmann is a former CEO of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and has held leadership roles at Pfizer and UCSF. Nicole Seligman is a corporate lawyer and former Sony executive with board roles at Paramount Global and others. Fidji Simo is CEO of Instacart and former Facebook executive. Their diverse backgrounds are expected to strengthen OpenAI's leadership and governance as the company expands.

item.title: Match Group adopts ChatGPT Enterprise to boost employee creativity, collaboration, and productivity across global teams [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Match Group, the company behind Tinder, Hinge, and OkCupid, has implemented ChatGPT Enterprise to enhance creativity and productivity among its employees. The AI tool is helping teams overcome language barriers, improve cross-functional collaboration, and accelerate product development. Employees use ChatGPT Enterprise for tasks such as prototyping without coding skills, running simulated user studies, fixing bugs, writing documentation, and translating for international collaboration. Match Group is also exploring custom GPTs to facilitate knowledge sharing and self-directed learning within the company. The company views its partnership with OpenAI as key to responsibly integrating AI into its operations and products, aiming to foster innovation and employee satisfaction while building better user experiences.

item.title: Paradigm uses OpenAI's GPT-4 to improve patient access and accuracy in clinical trial enrollment, reducing clinician workload and speeding data extraction [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Paradigm is leveraging OpenAI's GPT-4 API to enhance patient access to clinical trials by automating the evaluation of medical records, which traditionally slowed enrollment and limited trial participation. This approach aims to reduce clinician burnout and improve equitable access to trials, especially for underserved patients. GPT-4 outperformed specialized machine learning models and human experts in accuracy and speed, enabling Paradigm to extract new data elements in days instead of months and reduce expert validation time by 90%. The technology also supports regulatory compliance requirements such as HIPAA, facilitating integration with healthcare providers and accelerating Paradigm's expansion to new partners and trial types.

item.title: Lifespan uses GPT-4 to simplify surgical consent forms to a 6th grade reading level, improving patient understanding and well-being [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Lifespan, Rhode Island's largest healthcare system, has implemented GPT-4 technology to rewrite surgical consent forms from complex medical-legal language to a more accessible 6th grade reading level. This initiative aims to enhance health literacy and patient comfort by making medical information easier to understand. The process involves GPT-4 generating simplified drafts that are then reviewed by legal and medical experts to ensure accuracy. Since September 2023, Lifespan has deployed these shorter, clearer consent forms across its system, receiving positive feedback from patients and clinicians. The approach has expanded to other medical documents, including patient intake and chemotherapy consent forms, with the goal of empowering patients as informed healthcare consumers.

item.title: OpenAI details its early funding and split with Elon Musk, emphasizing mission to build safe AGI benefiting all humanity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has outlined its history with Elon Musk, noting that while Musk contributed less than $45 million compared to over $90 million from other donors, disagreements over control and funding led to his departure in 2018. The organization emphasized its commitment to building safe and beneficial artificial general intelligence (AGI) and distributing its benefits broadly. The company explained that initial plans for a $1 billion funding commitment evolved as they realized AGI development would require significantly more resources, prompting the creation of a for-profit entity. Musk proposed merging OpenAI with Tesla or taking majority control, but OpenAI declined to maintain its mission-focused governance. Despite Musk's exit and subsequent lawsuit, OpenAI continues to advance its mission by making AI tools widely accessible and useful across various sectors globally.

item.title: OpenAI releases Sora, a transformer-based diffusion model generating up to one-minute high-fidelity videos from text and images [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has developed Sora, a large-scale generative model that uses a transformer architecture to process spacetime patches of latent codes from both video and image data. Sora can generate high-quality videos up to one minute long, demonstrating the potential of scaling video generation models to create versatile simulators of the physical world. Sora operates by compressing visual data into a latent space and decomposing it into spacetime patches that serve as tokens for the transformer. Unlike prior models limited to fixed video sizes or durations, Sora can generate videos of variable lengths, resolutions, and aspect ratios, including widescreen and vertical formats. This flexibility improves composition and framing, enabling content generation tailored to different devices and use cases. The model is trained as a diffusion transformer that predicts clean patches from noisy inputs, showing improved sample quality with increased training compute. OpenAI suggests that this approach to video generation could pave the way for general-purpose simulators capable of modeling complex physical environments.

item.title: OpenAI and Microsoft disrupt five state-affiliated threat actors using AI for malicious cyber activities, terminating associated accounts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI, in collaboration with Microsoft Threat Intelligence, has disrupted five state-affiliated threat actors from China, Iran, North Korea, and Russia who attempted to misuse AI services for cyber operations. The actors used AI for tasks such as open-source research, coding assistance, and generating phishing content, leading to the termination of their OpenAI accounts. The disrupted groups included Charcoal Typhoon and Salmon Typhoon from China, Crimson Sandstorm from Iran, Emerald Sleet from North Korea, and Forest Blizzard from Russia. OpenAI emphasized that its models provide only limited incremental capabilities for malicious cybersecurity tasks compared to existing tools. The company outlined a multi-pronged approach involving monitoring, collaboration with industry partners, and iterative safety improvements to counter evolving threats from state-affiliated actors using AI.

item.title: OpenAI rolls out memory feature for ChatGPT with user controls for saved memories and chat history, enhancing personalization while maintaining privacy [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI is introducing a memory feature in ChatGPT that allows the AI to remember information from user conversations to provide more personalized and relevant responses over time. Users can control this feature by turning memory on or off, managing saved memories, or using temporary chats that do not retain information. The memory system works by combining "saved memories" explicitly requested by users and "chat history" insights gathered from past interactions. This feature is available to free, Plus, Pro, Team, Enterprise, and Edu users, with controls to review, delete, or modify what ChatGPT remembers. OpenAI emphasizes user privacy by allowing users to opt out of memory and by not training models on content from Team and Enterprise customers.

item.title: OpenAI develops evaluation framework to assess GPT-4's potential role in aiding biological threat creation, finding only mild, statistically insignificant accuracy improvements [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI is creating a framework to evaluate the risk that large language models like GPT-4 could assist in creating biological threats. A study involving 100 participants, including biology experts and students, compared performance using only the internet versus internet plus GPT-4 across tasks related to biological threat creation. The results showed mild improvements in accuracy and completeness for those with GPT-4 access, but these were not statistically significant, indicating limited current risk from the model alone. The evaluation measured five stages of biological threat creation and five performance metrics, aiming to establish a baseline for future research and community discussion. OpenAI emphasizes that access to information alone does not equate to successful threat creation and highlights the need for further research to determine meaningful risk thresholds and improve evaluation methods for AI-enabled biological risks.

item.title: OpenAI launches new text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-3-large models with improved performance and lower prices, updates GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4 Turbo models, and enhances API key management [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced two new embedding models, text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-3-large, offering stronger performance and reduced pricing compared to previous models. The company also updated its GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4 Turbo models, lowered GPT-3.5 Turbo prices, and added new API features for key management and usage tracking. Data sent to the API will not be used to train OpenAI models by default. The new embedding models provide significant improvements on benchmarks like MIRACL and MTEB, with the large model supporting up to 3072 dimensions and allowing developers to shorten embeddings to balance performance and cost. GPT-3.5 Turbo pricing has been cut by up to 50%, and the updated model fixes a text encoding bug affecting non-English function calls. These updates aim to enhance developer efficiency and scalability for AI integration.

item.title: OpenAI funds 10 international teams to develop democratic governance tools for AI and shares lessons and implementation plans [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI awarded $100,000 to 10 teams worldwide to design tools and methods for collective AI governance, aiming to incorporate public input into AI behavior aligned with human values. The program addressed challenges like diverse participant recruitment, transparent processes, and representing varied viewpoints. The selected teams, spanning 12 countries and multiple disciplines, developed innovations including video deliberation interfaces, crowdsourced AI audits, and mathematical models for representation. OpenAI plans to integrate these prototypes into an end-to-end process for collecting external stakeholder inputs to shape AI model behavior, continuing collaboration with researchers and engineers to advance democratic AI governance.

item.title: OpenAI implements safeguards to prevent misuse and promote transparency in AI-generated content for 2024 global elections [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI is taking multiple measures to prevent abuse of its AI technology during the 2024 worldwide elections, including directing users to authoritative voting information, blocking requests to generate images of real politicians, and monitoring for covert influence operations. The company has collaborated with organizations like the National Association of Secretaries of State and the European Parliament to provide reliable election resources through ChatGPT. In addition to these efforts, OpenAI has introduced tools to help identify AI-generated images and joined the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity to promote transparency. The company continues to test and adjust its safeguards as election day approaches, aiming to reduce misinformation and maintain neutrality in political content generated by its models.

item.title: Digital Green launches Farmer.Chat using OpenAI to support agricultural extension agents in India and Kenya, aiming to increase farmer income and reduce service costs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Digital Green has developed Farmer.Chat, an AI-powered chatbot built on OpenAI's GPT-4, to assist agricultural extension agents in India and Kenya by providing tailored, locally relevant farming advice. The tool integrates a vast database of training videos, call center logs, and research validated by India's Ministry of Agriculture to improve farmer support in remote communities. Farmer.Chat aims to reduce the cost of traditional extension services by up to 100 times and supports multiple languages including Hindi and Swahili. Over 4,500 extension agents are currently using the tool, which also offers features like crop diagnosis through photos and real-time weather and market updates. Digital Green plans to expand the rollout and enhance the chatbot's capabilities with specialized agricultural language models.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT Store for ChatGPT Plus, Team, and Enterprise users to discover and share custom GPT applications [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced the GPT Store, a platform that allows ChatGPT Plus, Team, and Enterprise users to explore and access a variety of GPT-based applications created by partners and the community. The store features popular and trending GPTs across categories like writing, programming, education, and lifestyle, with new featured GPTs highlighted weekly. Users can build and share their own GPTs without coding skills, subject to verification and compliance with OpenAI's usage policies. OpenAI plans to launch a GPT builder revenue program in Q1 2024, initially paying US builders based on user engagement. Team and Enterprise customers will have additional management controls for GPTs within their workspaces, with assurances that conversations are not used to improve OpenAI's models.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Team plan with advanced AI tools and secure collaboration features for businesses [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Team, a new subscription plan designed for teams to access advanced AI models like GPT-4 and DALL·E 3 within a secure, collaborative workspace. The plan includes admin tools, data privacy protections, and customization options to enhance productivity in professional settings. ChatGPT Team is priced at $25 per user per month when billed annually and offers early access to new features. The plan supports custom GPTs tailored to specific workflows, aiming to improve efficiency and work quality across various industries.

item.title: OpenAI says it supports journalism, collaborates with news organizations, and calls The New York Times lawsuit against it without merit [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has affirmed its support for journalism and detailed partnerships with various news organizations to enhance reporting and content access. The company also stated that it considers the lawsuit filed by The New York Times against it to be without merit and used the opportunity to clarify its business practices and technology development. OpenAI highlighted its efforts to work with news organizations by deploying AI tools that assist reporters, training models on diverse content including non-public sources, and providing real-time attributed news content in ChatGPT. The company emphasized that training AI on publicly available materials is fair use and offers publishers an opt-out option, which The New York Times adopted in August 2023. OpenAI acknowledged rare issues with content memorization in its models and said it is actively working to minimize such occurrences.

item.title: WHOOP integrates GPT-4 to deliver personalized fitness and health coaching through its wearable app [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: WHOOP has incorporated OpenAI's GPT-4 into its wearable companion app to provide personalized, on-demand fitness and health coaching. The AI-powered WHOOP Coach analyzes individual health data to answer user questions and offer tailored guidance on sleep, workouts, and stress management. This integration marks the first wearable to deliver highly individualized performance coaching using large language models, aiming to help users achieve their health goals more effectively.

item.title: Summer Health uses OpenAI's GPT-4 to automate pediatric visit notes, reducing doctor note-taking time by 80% and improving clarity for parents [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Summer Health has integrated OpenAI's GPT-4 to generate clear, jargon-free pediatric visit notes from doctors' observations, aiming to enhance documentation accuracy and reduce administrative burdens. This AI-assisted process allows pediatricians to cut note-taking time from 10 minutes to 2 minutes per visit, speeding up note completion and reducing fatigue. The new system includes a clinical review step to ensure medical accuracy and relevance. Parents have responded positively to the clearer, more accessible notes, reporting better understanding of their child's health and care plans. Summer Health plans to continue refining the model in collaboration with OpenAI to further improve pediatric care documentation.

item.title: OpenAI publishes initial best practices for governing agentic AI systems to ensure safety and accountability amid autonomous decision-making capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI released a white paper outlining recommended governance practices for agentic AI systems, which are capable of pursuing complex goals with limited supervision. The paper defines agentic AI, identifies responsible parties throughout the AI lifecycle, and proposes baseline safety and accountability measures to manage risks associated with autonomous AI agents. The document also discusses uncertainties in implementing these practices and highlights the need for additional governance frameworks to address indirect impacts from widespread adoption. OpenAI announced a now-closed research grant program funding studies on the safety and societal effects of agentic AI systems, aiming to support the development of responsible AI integration.

item.title: OpenAI and Eric Schmidt launch $10M Superalignment Fast Grants to fund research on aligning and safely overseeing superhuman AI systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI, in partnership with Eric Schmidt, has launched a $10 million grant program to support technical research aimed at aligning and ensuring the safety of superhuman AI systems. The initiative targets challenges such as weak-to-strong generalization, interpretability, and scalable oversight, which are critical as AI capabilities advance beyond human understanding. The program offers grants ranging from $100,000 to $2 million for academic labs, nonprofits, and individual researchers, along with a $150,000 fellowship for graduate students. Applications are open until February 18, and no prior alignment experience is required, reflecting the organizers' goal to attract new researchers to this emerging field. The grants focus on addressing fundamental problems in AI alignment that current methods like reinforcement learning from human feedback may not solve as AI systems become more complex and capable.

item.title: OpenAI researchers explore weak-to-strong generalization to align superhuman AI by using smaller models to supervise larger ones, showing GPT-2-level supervision can elicit near GPT-3.5 performance from GPT-4 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI's Superalignment team introduced a new research direction addressing the challenge of aligning superhuman AI systems by investigating whether smaller, less capable models can effectively supervise larger, more capable ones. Their experiments demonstrated that a GPT-2-level model could guide GPT-4 to perform at a level close to GPT-3.5, even generalizing correctly on difficult tasks where the smaller model failed. This approach aims to tackle the problem that humans will be weak supervisors relative to future superintelligent AI, making direct human oversight difficult. The team used methods encouraging the stronger model to confidently disagree with the weaker supervisor when appropriate, showing promising initial results despite limitations such as challenges with ChatGPT preference data. The research opens new empirical avenues for improving AI alignment as models grow more capable, though important differences remain between current experiments and future superhuman AI alignment challenges.

item.title: OpenAI and Axel Springer form global partnership to integrate AI in journalism, enhancing ChatGPT with recent news from Axel Springer's media brands [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI and Axel Springer have announced a global partnership to deepen the integration of AI technologies in journalism, aiming to strengthen independent journalism and improve user experience with ChatGPT. The collaboration will provide ChatGPT users worldwide with summaries of selected news content from Axel Springer's media brands, including POLITICO, BUSINESS INSIDER, BILD, and WELT, featuring attribution and links to full articles for transparency. The partnership also supports Axel Springer's AI-driven ventures built on OpenAI's technology and involves using Axel Springer's quality content to advance OpenAI's large language models. This initiative reflects both companies' commitment to leveraging AI to enhance content experiences and create sustainable financial opportunities for journalism.

item.title: OpenAI reinstates Sam Altman as CEO with new initial board including Bret Taylor, Larry Summers, and Adam D'Angelo [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Sam Altman has returned as CEO of OpenAI, with Mira Murati resuming her role as Chief Technology Officer and Greg Brockman returning as President. The company announced a new initial board composed of Bret Taylor as chair, Larry Summers, and Adam D'Angelo. Messages from Altman and board chair Taylor highlighted the leadership changes and expressed confidence in the company's future. Altman acknowledged the contributions of former board member Ilya Sutskever and others involved in the transition, emphasizing the team's resilience during a challenging period. He outlined immediate priorities including advancing research, investing in safety, and improving product deployment. The company also noted ongoing partnerships, including a non-voting observer role for Microsoft on the new board.

item.title: OpenAI appoints CTO Mira Murati as interim CEO after Sam Altman departs amid board confidence concerns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI announced that Sam Altman has left his role as CEO and the board of directors, with chief technology officer Mira Murati stepping in as interim CEO. The board cited a lack of consistent candor from Altman, which affected their confidence in his leadership, and has begun a search for a permanent successor. Murati, who has been with OpenAI for five years and leads research, product, and safety functions, is expected to provide stable leadership during the transition. The board emphasized its commitment to OpenAI's mission to ensure artificial general intelligence benefits all humanity, while Greg Brockman will step down as board chairman but remain with the company reporting to the CEO.

item.title: OpenAI launches Data Partnerships to create open-source and private datasets for AI training with global organizations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI announced its Data Partnerships initiative to collaborate with organizations in producing public and private datasets aimed at improving AI model training. The program seeks diverse, large-scale datasets across languages, topics, and formats to enhance AI understanding of human society and specialized domains. Partners include the Icelandic Government and Free Law Project, contributing curated legal and linguistic data to improve GPT-4's capabilities. OpenAI offers tools like OCR and speech recognition to help digitize and clean data, emphasizing privacy and sensitivity controls for private datasets. The initiative aims to broaden AI training data to support safer and more useful AI models, inviting organizations to contribute unique data that reflects their industries or cultures while advancing AI research and development.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPTs, enabling users to create and share custom ChatGPT versions with tailored instructions, knowledge, and skills [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced GPTs, a new feature that allows users to build customized versions of ChatGPT for specific tasks without coding. These GPTs can combine instructions, additional knowledge, and various capabilities such as web search, image generation, or data analysis, and can be shared publicly or used internally within organizations. The company plans to launch a GPT Store where verified creators can showcase their GPTs, which will be searchable and ranked by popularity. OpenAI emphasizes privacy and safety, ensuring user data control and reviewing GPTs against usage policies to prevent harmful content. Developers can also connect GPTs to external APIs to enable real-world interactions, and enterprise customers can deploy internal-only GPTs for their organizations.

item.title: OpenAI announces GPT-4 Turbo with 128K context, Assistants API, GPT-4 Turbo with Vision, and DALL·E 3 API at DevDay [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI unveiled several new models and developer products at DevDay, including GPT-4 Turbo with a 128K token context window and reduced pricing, the Assistants API for building AI assistants, GPT-4 Turbo with Vision capabilities, and the DALL·E 3 API. These updates aim to enhance multimodal AI capabilities and developer tools across the platform. GPT-4 Turbo offers improved performance and knowledge up to April 2023, with a context window that can handle over 300 pages of text and is priced significantly lower than previous versions. The Assistants API enables developers to create AI applications with specific goals that can call models and tools, while new features like function calling improvements, JSON mode, and reproducible outputs provide greater control and accuracy for developers.

item.title: OpenAI builds Preparedness team and launches challenge to address catastrophic risks from highly-capable frontier AI systems [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI is enhancing its approach to managing catastrophic risks associated with highly-capable AI by establishing a new Preparedness team led by Aleksander Madry and launching an AI Preparedness Challenge. The team will focus on evaluating, forecasting, and mitigating risks such as individualized persuasion, cybersecurity threats, and chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear dangers related to frontier AI models. The Preparedness team aims to develop a Risk-Informed Development Policy to guide rigorous capability evaluations, monitoring, and protective actions for frontier AI systems. The AI Preparedness Challenge invited submissions to identify novel risk areas, awarding $25,000 in API credits to top entries, which helped surface new types of risks and informed OpenAI's safety and mitigation strategies for future AI developments.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft appoint Chris Meserole as Frontier Model Forum Executive Director and launch $10 million AI Safety Fund [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft have named Chris Meserole as the first Executive Director of the Frontier Model Forum, an industry group focused on the safe and responsible development of advanced AI models. They also announced a new AI Safety Fund with over $10 million in initial funding from these companies and philanthropic partners to support research on AI safety and evaluation techniques. Meserole brings extensive experience in technology policy and AI governance, previously leading the AI and Emerging Technology Initiative at the Brookings Institution. The AI Safety Fund aims to support independent researchers worldwide in developing new methods for testing and red teaming frontier AI models to identify and mitigate potential risks. The fund will be administered by the Meridian Institute with guidance from an advisory committee of experts.

item.title: OpenAI integrates DALL·E 3 into ChatGPT Plus and Enterprise with new safety and provenance features [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has launched DALL·E 3 within ChatGPT Plus and Enterprise, enabling users to generate and refine images through conversation. The release includes a multi-tiered safety system to prevent harmful content and limits on generating images in the style of living artists or public figures. OpenAI is also developing a provenance classifier to identify AI-generated images with over 99% accuracy in internal tests, aiming to improve transparency and trust in AI-generated content.

item.title: Typeform launches Formless AI platform using GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 to create dynamic, conversational data collection without traditional forms [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Typeform has introduced Formless, an AI-powered platform built on OpenAI's GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4 models, designed to transform online forms into interactive, conversational experiences. Instead of traditional form structures, Formless allows businesses to collect data through natural, two-way conversations that adapt based on respondent answers and support multiple languages. The platform enables form creators to train the AI on specific topics and customize responses to match brand tone, while respondents can ask follow-up questions as in a real dialogue. Formless also includes AI-driven tools for analyzing conversational data and integrating insights, aiming to simplify data collection and interpretation for businesses at scale.

item.title: Retool integrates GPT-4 to enable businesses to build AI-powered apps faster and more securely [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Retool has integrated OpenAI's GPT-4 into its platform to help businesses quickly develop AI-powered applications that improve operational efficiency. The new Retool AI suite offers pre-built AI actions and templates, allowing teams to create custom AI-driven workflows for various business processes such as inventory management and customer support. Retool aims to make AI more accessible by turning common AI tasks into visual building blocks that can be assembled without extensive coding. The integration supports secure data governance and is expected to expand with additional AI capabilities and templates to accelerate AI adoption in business applications.

item.title: Ironclad integrates GPT-4 to automate contract review with AI Assist™, reducing review time from 40 minutes to two minutes [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Ironclad, a contract lifecycle management platform, has incorporated GPT-4 technology into its AI Assist™ tool to streamline contract review processes. This integration enables automated identification and redlining of contract irregularities, supports company-specific language guidelines, and allows users to control AI suggestions with human oversight. Since launching the beta in March 2023 and upgrading to GPT-4 in April, AI Assist™ has become one of Ironclad's most rapidly adopted features, significantly boosting legal team efficiency without replacing human judgment. The platform ensures data privacy by default, with OpenAI not using submitted data to train its models.

item.title: OpenAI releases DALL·E 3 system card detailing model capabilities, risks, and safety measures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has published the system card for DALL·E 3, outlining the model's improved image generation quality and caption fidelity compared to DALL·E 2. The document includes information on external expert evaluations, risk assessments, and mitigations implemented to reduce unwanted behaviors and enhance safe deployment. The system card aims to increase transparency about DALL·E 3's design and operational considerations, providing guidance for responsible use of the AI image generation system.

item.title: OpenAI rolls out ChatGPT voice and image capabilities for Plus and Enterprise users, enabling multimodal interactions on iOS, Android, and other platforms [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced new voice and image features in ChatGPT, allowing users to engage in spoken conversations and share images for analysis. These capabilities are being gradually deployed to Plus and Enterprise users across mobile and desktop platforms, enhancing the AI's usability for tasks like meal planning, troubleshooting, and educational assistance. The voice feature uses a new text-to-speech model with human-like audio generated from text and sample speech, supported by Whisper for speech recognition. Image understanding is powered by multimodal GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 models, which can interpret photographs, screenshots, and documents. OpenAI is implementing these features cautiously to address risks such as impersonation and hallucinations, informed by collaborations with voice actors and accessibility organizations.

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-4V system card detailing multimodal capabilities, safety evaluations, and intended use cases for vision-enabled GPT-4 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has published the system card for GPT-4V(ision), its latest multimodal model that integrates image understanding with language processing. The document outlines the model's capabilities, performance metrics, safety considerations, and guidance for users to effectively leverage its ability to analyze and respond to image and text inputs. The system card builds on prior safety work done for GPT-4 and provides deeper analysis specific to image inputs, reflecting OpenAI's efforts to address risks and ensure responsible deployment of vision-enabled AI technology.

item.title: OpenAI launches Red Teaming Network to engage experts in improving AI model safety [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has established the OpenAI Red Teaming Network, inviting domain experts worldwide to collaborate on assessing and enhancing the safety of its AI models. The network aims to provide ongoing, diverse input throughout the model development lifecycle rather than one-off evaluations before deployments. The initiative seeks experts from various fields including cognitive science, cybersecurity, law, and healthcare, among others, to participate in red teaming projects that may require limited time commitments annually. Members will be compensated for their contributions and may be subject to confidentiality agreements. Applications for the initial phase closed in December 2023, with potential future rounds planned.

item.title: OpenAI opens new office in Dublin to expand European operations and support AI development [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has established a new office in Dublin, Ireland, as part of its strategy to grow its presence in Europe. The Dublin office will focus on operations, trust and safety, go-to-market, security engineering, and legal work to better serve the European market. The company plans to build a team throughout the year and collaborate with the Irish government, industry, startups, and researchers to support Ireland's National AI Strategy. OpenAI has also begun providing access to its technology and mentorship to local youth programs, aiming to contribute to Ireland's growing tech ecosystem and AI innovation efforts.

item.title: OpenAI announces first developer conference, DevDay, on November 6 in San Francisco with in-person registration opening soon and keynote livestream available globally [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI will hold its first developer conference, DevDay, on November 6, 2023, in San Francisco, bringing together hundreds of developers to preview new tools and participate in breakout sessions led by OpenAI's technical staff. The event aims to showcase the latest advancements in OpenAI's API, which is currently used by over 2 million developers worldwide for applications involving GPT-4, GPT-3.5, DALL·E, and Whisper. Registration for in-person attendance will open in the coming weeks, and the keynote will be livestreamed for developers globally. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman highlighted the company's focus on enabling developers to build new applications using their technology.

item.title: OpenAI releases guide for teachers on using ChatGPT in classrooms, including prompts, AI limitations, detection tools, and bias discussions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has published a guide to help educators integrate ChatGPT into their teaching, offering suggested prompts, explanations of how the AI works and its limitations, insights on AI detection tools, and discussions about potential biases. The guide includes examples of how teachers use ChatGPT for role-playing, creating quizzes and lesson plans, supporting non-English speakers, and fostering critical thinking among students. It also provides resources and FAQs to assist educators in responsibly incorporating AI tools into their classrooms.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Enterprise with enhanced security, unlimited fast GPT-4 access, and advanced data analysis for business use [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Enterprise, a version of ChatGPT designed for businesses with enterprise-grade security and privacy features, including SOC 2 compliance and data encryption. It offers unlimited, faster access to GPT-4, longer context windows, advanced data analysis tools, and customization options to support large-scale deployment and collaboration within organizations. Since ChatGPT's launch, over 80% of Fortune 500 companies have adopted it, prompting OpenAI to create a secure, scalable solution for enterprises. Early adopters like Block, Canva, and PwC use ChatGPT Enterprise to improve productivity across tasks such as coding, communication, and data analysis. The platform ensures that customer data is not used for model training and provides administrative controls like single sign-on and usage analytics. ChatGPT Enterprise aims to enhance workplace productivity by enabling teams to handle complex queries and workflows securely. OpenAI plans to add more features, including customization that integrates company data and applications, to further tailor the AI assistant for organizational needs.

item.title: OpenAI partners with Scale to support enterprise fine-tuning of GPT-3.5 Turbo and upcoming GPT-4 models [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has partnered with Scale to help enterprises customize its advanced AI models through fine-tuning, enabling companies to tailor models securely on proprietary data. This collaboration leverages Scale's expertise in data enrichment and model evaluation to enhance enterprise-grade AI deployment. Fine-tuning is currently available for GPT-3.5 Turbo, with plans to extend it to GPT-4 later in the year, allowing customers to maintain ownership of their data without it being used to train other models.

item.title: OpenAI launches fine-tuning for GPT-3.5 Turbo with API updates, enabling customized models and improved performance for developers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced fine-tuning capabilities for GPT-3.5 Turbo, allowing developers to customize the model using their own data to better suit specific use cases. This update includes API enhancements and promises improved model performance, including better instruction following, output formatting, and tone customization. Fine-tuning for GPT-4 is expected later this fall. The fine-tuning process supports up to 4,000 tokens and can reduce prompt sizes by up to 90%, which speeds up API calls and lowers costs. OpenAI ensures safety by screening training data through moderation systems. Pricing includes separate costs for training and usage tokens. Additionally, OpenAI has updated GPT-3 base models with replacements available and deprecated older API endpoints effective January 2024.

item.title: OpenAI acquires Global Illumination, integrating its entire team to work on core products including ChatGPT [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has acquired Global Illumination, a company known for leveraging AI to build creative tools and digital experiences. The entire Global Illumination team, which includes founders with experience at Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, Google, Pixar, and Riot Games, has joined OpenAI to contribute to its core products such as ChatGPT.

item.title: OpenAI uses GPT-4 to improve content moderation by enabling faster policy development, consistent labeling, and reducing human moderator workload [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI is applying GPT-4 to content moderation and policy development to achieve more consistent content labeling, accelerate policy refinement feedback loops, and lessen reliance on human moderators. This approach shortens the policy update cycle from months to hours and allows the model to interpret complex policy documents and adapt instantly to changes. The process involves policy experts creating labeled datasets, which GPT-4 then labels independently; discrepancies are analyzed to refine policies iteratively. This method aims to reduce the mental burden on human moderators by automating the review of harmful content and offers a scalable solution for digital platforms. OpenAI encourages others with API access to implement similar AI-assisted moderation systems and is exploring enhancements like chain-of-thought reasoning and risk detection to further improve moderation quality.

item.title: OpenAI and UC Berkeley host workshop on confidence-building measures for AI to address international security risks from foundation models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI's Geopolitics Team and the Berkeley Risk and Security Lab convened a workshop to explore confidence-building measures (CBMs) aimed at mitigating risks posed by foundation AI models to global security. The workshop gathered multiple stakeholders to discuss strategies such as crisis hotlines, incident sharing, transparency tools, content provenance, collaborative red teaming, and dataset sharing to reduce conflict and build trust in AI development and deployment. The proceedings highlight that many foundation model developers are non-governmental, requiring broad stakeholder involvement to implement these CBMs effectively. These measures, rooted in Cold War-era practices, are proposed as flexible tools to navigate rapid changes in AI capabilities and to prevent accidents, escalation, and misuse that could undermine state security.

item.title: Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI launch Frontier Model Forum to promote safe and responsible development of advanced AI models [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI have formed the Frontier Model Forum, an industry organization aimed at advancing AI safety research, establishing best practices, and facilitating information sharing among policymakers and industry stakeholders. The Forum focuses on ensuring the responsible development of frontier AI models, defined as large-scale models exceeding current capabilities, and supports collaboration to address societal challenges such as climate change and healthcare. The Forum plans to create an advisory board, develop public libraries of technical evaluations and benchmarks, and coordinate research on AI safety topics including adversarial robustness and anomaly detection. Membership is open to organizations committed to frontier model safety and willing to contribute to joint initiatives, with the goal of fostering cross-sector cooperation to mitigate risks associated with advanced AI systems.

item.title: OpenAI and leading AI labs commit to voluntary safety and transparency measures to advance AI governance coordinated by the White House [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI and other prominent AI research labs have announced a set of voluntary commitments aimed at enhancing the safety, security, and trustworthiness of advanced AI technologies. This initiative, coordinated by the White House, seeks to establish meaningful governance practices for highly capable AI models, including ongoing research and red-teaming efforts to assess and mitigate risks. The commitments focus on internal and external red-teaming to address misuse, societal risks, and national security concerns such as bio, cyber, and radiological threats. Companies also pledge to share information on emerging risks and collaborate on developing shared safety standards and best practices. These voluntary measures are intended to complement existing laws and remain in effect until formal regulations covering similar issues are enacted.

item.title: OpenAI launches custom instructions feature for ChatGPT to apply user preferences across all future conversations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a custom instructions feature for ChatGPT that allows users to set preferences or requirements for how the AI responds, which will be applied to all future interactions. This feature is initially available in beta for Plus plan users and will expand to all users soon, excluding the UK and EU for now. The update aims to reduce the need for users to repeat information in each conversation and improve the experience with plugins by sharing relevant user details automatically. OpenAI has adapted safety and privacy measures to handle these new instructions, including moderation to prevent policy violations and options to control data usage for model improvement.

item.title: OpenAI commits $5 million and API credits to American Journalism Project to explore AI applications in local news [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has partnered with the American Journalism Project (AJP) to invest over $5 million and provide up to $5 million in API credits to support the use of artificial intelligence in local news organizations. The collaboration aims to help local news outlets innovate with AI tools while addressing challenges such as misinformation and bias. The partnership will fund a technology and AI studio to assist AJP's portfolio organizations in experimenting with AI applications, provide direct grants to about ten local news groups for pilot projects, and foster a feedback loop between the local news sector and AI developers. This initiative seeks to strengthen local journalism's role in democracy by promoting responsible AI adoption and combating disinformation.

item.title: Viable uses GPT-4 to analyze large-scale qualitative data with high accuracy, enabling faster, nuanced insights for customer feedback and support [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Viable has developed a platform that leverages GPT-4 to analyze unstructured qualitative data at scale, providing businesses with accurate and actionable insights from customer feedback and support interactions. This approach goes beyond simple summarization by adding context to better understand sentiment and nuances such as sarcasm and negation. The platform integrates with tools like Zendesk and Intercom to categorize data into themes, track trends over time, and identify churn risks, helping companies improve Net Promoter Scores and reduce support ticket volumes. Viable's use of fine-tuned large language models has saved customers significant time and resources while enhancing decision-making based on comprehensive qualitative data.

item.title: OpenAI outlines regulatory framework for frontier AI to manage public safety risks with standards, reporting, and compliance mechanisms [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI published a white paper proposing a regulatory approach for frontier AI models, which are highly capable foundation models that could pose severe public safety risks. The paper emphasizes the need for standard-setting, registration and reporting requirements, and compliance mechanisms to address challenges such as unexpected dangerous capabilities and misuse. The authors suggest industry self-regulation as a first step but call for broader societal and government involvement to establish and enforce safety standards. Proposed measures include pre-deployment risk assessments, external scrutiny, informed deployment decisions, and ongoing monitoring of AI capabilities and uses after deployment to balance innovation benefits with public safety concerns.

item.title: OpenAI shares insights from global conversations across 22 countries to guide future AI development and deployment strategies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI conducted a four-week global tour led by CEO Sam Altman, engaging with users, developers, policymakers, and the public in 25 cities across six continents to gather diverse perspectives on AI. The discussions highlighted both enthusiasm for AI's potential in education, healthcare, and economic growth, and concerns about misinformation, economic displacement, and safety risks. The feedback emphasized the need for accessible, culturally aware AI products and ongoing dialogue with policymakers focused on safe deployment and regulation. OpenAI plans to enhance product usefulness, improve language performance, maintain accessible pricing, and continue investing in safety mechanisms based on these global insights.

item.title: OpenAI opens its first international office in London to expand research, engineering, and policy efforts in AGI development [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has launched its first international office in London, United Kingdom, marking a significant step in its global expansion beyond the United States. The new office aims to broaden OpenAI's research and development capabilities and engage with local communities and policymakers to advance safe artificial general intelligence (AGI). The London team will focus on research, engineering, and go-to-market functions, leveraging the city's rich talent pool and technology ecosystem to drive innovation in AGI development and policy.

item.title: OpenAI updates API with function calling, more steerable GPT-4 and GPT-3.5-turbo models, 16k context length, and reduced pricing [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI announced several API updates including new function calling capabilities in the Chat Completions API, more steerable versions of GPT-4 and GPT-3.5-turbo, a 16k context length version of GPT-3.5-turbo, and significant price reductions. The updates aim to improve instruction following, factual accuracy, and integration with external tools through structured JSON outputs for function calls. The function calling feature allows developers to define functions that the models can invoke by outputting JSON arguments, enabling applications like chatbots that interact with external APIs, converting natural language into API calls or database queries, and extracting structured data from text. OpenAI also extended support for older model versions until at least June 2024 and emphasized data privacy guarantees, with customer data not used for training.

item.title: OpenAI launches $1M Cybersecurity Grant Program to support AI-powered defensive cybersecurity tools and research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a $1 million Cybersecurity Grant Program aimed at advancing AI-driven cybersecurity capabilities for defenders. The program offers funding, API credits, and other support to projects focused on practical AI applications in defensive cybersecurity, excluding offensive security efforts. OpenAI seeks to empower defenders, measure AI cybersecurity capabilities, and foster discourse on AI and cybersecurity challenges. The program encourages proposals that enhance defensive tools such as incident triage automation, vulnerability patching, threat intelligence, and secure software development. Grants are awarded in increments of $10,000, prioritizing projects intended for broad public benefit and sharing. OpenAI updated the program in 2026 to emphasize large-scale deployment of its models, including a $10 million commitment in API credits with the release of GPT-5.3-Codex and Trusted Access for Cyber.

item.title: OpenAI shows process supervision improves mathematical reasoning models by rewarding each correct step, boosting performance and alignment with human reasoning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has developed a training method called process supervision that rewards each correct step in mathematical problem solving rather than only the final answer. This approach improves model performance on the MATH dataset and aligns the model's reasoning process more closely with human-endorsed chains of thought. Compared to traditional outcome supervision, process supervision produces more reliable and interpretable reasoning without sacrificing accuracy. The research suggests potential for broader application beyond math, encouraging further exploration of process supervision in other domains.

item.title: OpenAI launches $1 million grant program to fund experiments in democratic rule-setting for AI systems within legal frameworks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI, Inc. is awarding ten grants of $100,000 each to support projects that develop democratic processes for deciding the rules AI systems should follow, aiming to incorporate diverse public perspectives within legal boundaries. The initiative seeks to explore how AI governance can reflect societal values beyond existing laws, addressing questions about AI behavior and representation of disputed views. The program encourages innovative approaches to democratic decision-making, including deliberation and transparent outcomes, while acknowledging challenges such as representation and manipulation risks. OpenAI views this effort as a complement to government regulation and aims to use the results to inform future, broader democratic oversight of advanced AI systems.

item.title: OpenAI outlines initial proposals for governance of superintelligence to manage risks and ensure safety as AI capabilities approach and exceed expert human levels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI emphasizes the need to begin governance discussions for superintelligence-AI systems far surpassing artificial general intelligence-anticipating their significant impact within the next decade. The organization highlights the potential for both great benefits and existential risks, urging proactive coordination and safety measures. The proposals include international coordination among leading AI developers, the establishment of an oversight body similar to the IAEA to monitor and regulate high-capability AI efforts, and advancing technical research to ensure superintelligence safety. OpenAI also stresses the importance of public oversight and democratic input on AI deployment, while allowing less capable AI models to develop with fewer restrictions. The goal is to balance innovation with risk mitigation as AI technologies evolve rapidly.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT app for iOS with conversation syncing, voice input, and GPT-4 access for Plus subscribers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has released the ChatGPT app for iOS, offering features like syncing conversation history across devices, voice input powered by its Whisper speech-recognition system, and access to GPT-4 capabilities for ChatGPT Plus subscribers. The app is free to use and initially available in the US, with plans to expand to other countries and eventually to Android devices. OpenAI aims to continuously improve the app based on user feedback while making advanced AI tools more accessible.

item.title: OpenAI uses GPT-4 to generate and score explanations for every neuron in GPT-2, releasing a dataset of these imperfect neuron behavior explanations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI employed GPT-4 to automatically produce and evaluate natural language explanations for the behavior of individual neurons in the GPT-2 language model, releasing a dataset covering all 307,200 neurons. This approach aims to scale interpretability research by automating the understanding of neural components, which traditionally required manual inspection and does not scale well for large models. The study found that while most explanations scored poorly, improvements were possible by iterating explanations, using larger explainer models, and modifying model architectures. Over 1,000 neurons received high-scoring explanations, though many interesting neurons remain poorly understood. OpenAI acknowledges limitations such as the complexity of neuron behavior, the focus on individual neurons rather than circuits, and the compute intensity of the method, and hopes the research community will build on this work to develop better interpretability tools.

item.title: OpenAI adds chat history toggle in ChatGPT to let users control data used for model training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a feature in ChatGPT that allows users to disable chat history, preventing those conversations from being used to train AI models and from appearing in the history sidebar. This setting can be changed at any time and aims to simplify data management compared to previous opt-out processes. Conversations with chat history disabled are retained for 30 days for abuse monitoring before deletion. Additionally, OpenAI is developing a ChatGPT Business subscription for professionals and enterprises that will follow stricter data usage policies, ensuring user data is not used for model training by default. The company also added a new Export option to make it easier for users to download their ChatGPT data and understand what information is stored.

item.title: OpenAI launches Bug Bounty Program to reward security researchers for identifying vulnerabilities in its AI systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a Bug Bounty Program inviting security researchers, ethical hackers, and technology enthusiasts to report vulnerabilities in its AI technologies. The program aims to enhance the safety and reliability of OpenAI's systems by leveraging external expertise to identify and address security flaws. The program is managed in partnership with Bugcrowd and offers cash rewards ranging from $200 to $20,000 based on the severity of reported issues. OpenAI emphasizes collaboration and transparency in its commitment to secure AI and encourages participation from the global security community.

item.title: OpenAI outlines its approach to AI safety, emphasizing rigorous testing, gradual deployment, and real-world learning to mitigate risks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI emphasizes the importance of building, deploying, and using AI systems safely as a core part of its mission. The organization conducts extensive testing, engages external experts, and uses techniques like reinforcement learning with human feedback to improve model safety before public release. It also advocates for regulation to ensure safety practices are widely adopted. OpenAI gradually releases AI models with safeguards and monitors real-world use to address misuse and improve policies. The company prioritizes protecting children by restricting access based on age, preventing harmful content generation, and collaborating with partners like Khan Academy on tailored safety measures. OpenAI also respects user privacy by using data to enhance model helpfulness without selling or profiling individuals.

item.title: OpenAI patches ChatGPT outage caused by redis-py bug that exposed some users' chat titles and limited payment info on March 20 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: On March 20, ChatGPT experienced an outage due to a bug in the redis-py open-source library that caused some users to see other users' chat titles and, for a small subset of ChatGPT Plus subscribers, limited payment information. OpenAI identified and patched the bug, restored service and chat history except for a few hours, and notified affected users about the exposure. The issue arose from a connection handling flaw in the Asyncio redis-py client used with Redis Cluster, which was triggered by a server change causing request cancellations. OpenAI has worked with redis-py maintainers to fix the bug and emphasized its commitment to user privacy and data security.

item.title: OpenAI launches initial plugin support for ChatGPT to enable access to current information and third-party services with safety as a core principle [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced initial support for plugins in ChatGPT, allowing the language model to access up-to-date information, perform computations, and use third-party services. These plugins are designed with safety in mind and are being gradually rolled out to a small set of users and developers from a waitlist. The first plugins come from partners including Expedia, Instacart, Shopify, Slack, Wolfram, and others, alongside OpenAI's own web browser and code interpreter plugins.
