OpenAI plans to expand access over time while studying real-world use, safety, and alignment challenges to improve the system and enable broader developer integration beyond ChatGPT.

item.title: OpenAI study finds GPT models could affect at least 10% of tasks for 80% of US workers, with 19% facing 50% task impact across wage levels [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study by OpenAI and University of Pennsylvania researchers assesses the potential impact of Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) models on the US labor market. It estimates that about 80% of workers could see at least 10% of their tasks influenced by GPTs, while 19% might have half or more of their tasks affected, spanning all income levels and industries. The research uses a new rubric combining human expertise and GPT-4 classifications to evaluate occupations' susceptibility to GPT capabilities. It highlights that GPTs exhibit traits of general-purpose technologies, implying significant economic, social, and policy implications as these models become more integrated into the workforce.

item.title: Be My Eyes integrates GPT-4 to enhance visual accessibility with AI-powered virtual volunteer for blind and low vision users [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Be My Eyes, a Danish startup supporting over 250 million blind or low vision users, has integrated GPT-4 technology to develop a Virtual Volunteer within its app that provides advanced visual assistance. This AI-powered tool can recognize and analyze images, enabling users to perform tasks like identifying objects, navigating environments, and accessing complex web content more independently. The GPT-4 integration allows conversational interaction and deeper analysis beyond basic image recognition, such as interpreting ingredients in a fridge or summarizing cluttered web pages for easier navigation. Beta testing with employees has shown positive results, and the feature is expected to be available to users soon, potentially transforming accessibility and independence for the visually impaired community.

item.title: Stripe uses GPT-4 to enhance developer support, improve business understanding, and strengthen fraud detection across its platform [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Stripe has integrated OpenAI's GPT-4 technology to improve various aspects of its payment platform, including developer support, business classification, and fraud detection. The company mobilized 100 employees to prototype GPT-4-powered features, identifying 50 potential AI use cases and selecting 15 for integration. GPT-4 outperformed human reviewers in summarizing business websites and helps answer technical support questions by analyzing documentation. Additionally, Stripe uses GPT-4 to monitor its community forums for malicious activity by analyzing communication patterns to flag potential fraudsters. The company is exploring further applications of GPT-4, such as providing business coaching and strategic advice, as the technology continues to advance.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-4, a large multimodal model processing text and images with human-level performance on professional and academic tests [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced GPT-4, a large multimodal deep learning model that accepts both image and text inputs and generates text outputs. While it is less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios, GPT-4 achieves human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks, including scoring in the top 10% on a simulated bar exam compared to GPT-3.5's bottom 10% score. The model was developed over six months with iterative alignment improvements and trained on a custom supercomputer co-designed with Azure. GPT-4 is available via ChatGPT and API for text inputs, with image input capabilities currently in research preview and limited release. OpenAI also open-sourced its evaluation framework, OpenAI Evals, to facilitate ongoing model assessment and improvement.

item.title: Duolingo integrates GPT-4 to enhance conversational practice and grammar explanations in new Duolingo Max subscription [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Duolingo has integrated OpenAI's GPT-4 into its language learning platform to provide more immersive conversation practice and contextual grammar feedback through new features called Role Play and Explain my Answer, available in the Duolingo Max subscription. These AI-powered tools aim to fill gaps in language acquisition by enabling free-flowing conversations and dynamic explanations tailored to learners' mistakes. The integration leverages GPT-4's improved accuracy over previous models to offer personalized, gamified learning experiences in Spanish and French, with plans to expand to additional languages. Duolingo's engineering team noted that GPT-4 has accelerated development and simplified testing, allowing faster rollout of advanced AI features that support both implicit and explicit language learning methods.

item.title: Khan Academy pilots GPT-4-powered Khanmigo AI assistant to personalize virtual education and support teachers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Khan Academy is conducting a limited pilot program using GPT-4 technology to power Khanmigo, an AI assistant designed to provide personalized tutoring for students and classroom support for teachers. The nonprofit aims to address diverse learning needs by enabling individualized questions and deeper conceptual understanding. The pilot began testing GPT-4 in 2022 and invites public waitlist participation. Khan Academy is also exploring GPT-4's potential to help teachers create instructional materials and monitor student progress, with a focus on responsible AI use and error correction during early trials.

item.title: Iceland partners with OpenAI to use GPT-4 for preserving and promoting the Icelandic language amid digitalization challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Iceland has partnered with OpenAI to leverage GPT-4 in efforts to preserve and promote the Icelandic language, which faces risks due to widespread use of English and digitalization. The initiative, supported by the Icelandic government and private industry, aims to integrate AI technology to maintain Icelandic as the country's default language and protect its cultural heritage. The project involves training GPT-4 with human feedback to improve its Icelandic language capabilities, addressing issues like grammatical errors and cultural inaccuracies. This approach uses reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) with a team of volunteers to fine-tune the model efficiently, creating a potential blueprint for preserving other low-resource languages. The effort also seeks to ensure AI supports both cultural preservation and economic prosperity in Iceland.

item.title: OpenAI outlines mission to develop artificial general intelligence that benefits all humanity while managing risks and ensuring broad access [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI's mission is to create artificial general intelligence (AGI) that surpasses human intelligence and benefits all of humanity. The organization aims to carefully develop and deploy AGI to maximize positive impact while minimizing risks such as misuse and societal disruption. OpenAI emphasizes a gradual transition to AGI, deploying increasingly powerful and aligned models to learn and adapt safely. The approach includes promoting broad access to AI technologies to encourage decentralized innovation and equitable benefit sharing, while exercising caution as systems approach AGI capabilities.

item.title: OpenAI outlines principles shaping ChatGPT behavior and plans to enhance customization and public input [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has detailed how ChatGPT's behavior is shaped through a two-step process involving pre-training on broad internet data and fine-tuning with human reviewers following specific guidelines. The company acknowledges current limitations and biases in the system and emphasizes ongoing efforts to improve alignment with human values. OpenAI plans to allow greater user customization of ChatGPT's behavior and increase public participation in decisions about the AI's conduct. The company also shares portions of its reviewer guidelines to promote transparency and accountability in addressing biases and controversial topics.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Plus subscription for $20/month with faster responses and priority access to new features [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Plus, a subscription plan offering general access to ChatGPT even during peak times, faster response times, and priority access to new features. The plan is available globally for $20 per month, while free access to ChatGPT remains available to all users. OpenAI aims to use the subscription revenue to support free access and plans to expand offerings based on user feedback, including exploring lower-cost and business plans.

item.title: OpenAI launches AI text classifier with limited accuracy to identify AI-generated content, discontinued as of July 2023 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduced a classifier designed to distinguish AI-written text from human-written text, aiming to help mitigate misinformation and academic dishonesty. The tool was publicly available for feedback but was discontinued in July 2023 due to its low accuracy, correctly identifying only 26% of AI-generated text and mislabeling 9% of human text as AI-written. The classifier was trained on paired datasets of human and AI-generated text and performed better on longer English texts but was unreliable on short texts, other languages, and code. OpenAI emphasized that the tool should not be used as a primary decision-making resource and highlighted ongoing research into more effective methods for detecting AI-generated content. The company also engaged with educators and other stakeholders to understand the impact and limitations of such detection tools.

item.title: OpenAI and Microsoft extend multi-year, multi-billion dollar partnership to advance AI research and deployment with Azure as exclusive cloud provider [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI and Microsoft announced a multi-year, multi-billion dollar extension of their partnership to continue independent AI research and development. Microsoft will increase investment in Azure-powered supercomputing systems, which remain the exclusive cloud provider for OpenAI's research, API, and products. The collaboration includes deploying OpenAI's technology through the Azure OpenAI Service and integrating AI into applications like GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Designer. Both companies also work together on safety and best practices to ensure AI systems are useful and broadly beneficial.

item.title: OpenAI, Georgetown, and Stanford publish report on risks of language models in disinformation campaigns and propose mitigation framework [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI collaborated with Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technology and the Stanford Internet Observatory to study how large language models could be misused in disinformation campaigns. Their joint research included a 2021 workshop with experts from multiple fields and resulted in a report outlining potential threats to information integrity and a framework for reducing these risks. The report examines how language models might lower costs and increase scale for influence operations by enabling new actors and tactics, such as real-time content generation and more persuasive messaging. It also discusses critical unknowns about future capabilities, actor intentions, and the diffusion of AI tools, emphasizing the need for further research and policy development to mitigate potential harms.

item.title: Yabble uses OpenAI's GPT-3 to rapidly analyze customer feedback and deliver nuanced business insights [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Yabble has integrated OpenAI's GPT-3 to accelerate the analysis of large customer feedback data sets, enabling faster and more detailed insights to inform business strategies. The AI-powered tools transform unstructured data into relevant themes and subthemes within minutes, significantly reducing the manual effort previously required. Since adopting GPT-3, Yabble's platform can handle more complex user queries and provide more relevant insights, making its AI-driven analysis essential for clients seeking to understand customer sentiment and improve products or services. This integration allows Yabble to scale its offerings and focus creative energy on expanding its capabilities.

item.title: Waymark fine-tunes GPT-3 to generate tailored video scripts, improving efficiency and relevance for automated video ad creation [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Waymark has integrated fine-tuned GPT-3 models into its video creation platform to produce custom marketing scripts quickly, addressing previous challenges with generic and time-consuming scriptwriting. This enhancement allows users to receive original, relevant scripts in seconds, reducing editing time and making video creation more accessible for businesses without technical expertise. Since its 2017 launch, Waymark has offered an easy-to-use platform for creating TV commercials and digital ads using professionally produced templates. The addition of GPT-3 transforms the service from a do-it-yourself tool to a done-for-you model, enabling companies, especially those working with local businesses, to save time and costs while improving the quality of their video marketing content.

item.title: OpenAI researchers use GPT-3 to develop advanced AI characters for improved interactivity and realism in digital environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI researchers are applying GPT-3 technology to create next-generation AI-powered characters designed to enhance interactivity and realism in digital settings. This work aims to advance the capabilities of digital characters by leveraging large language models to simulate more natural and engaging behaviors.

item.title: OpenAI researcher Lilian Weng highlights continuous learning and teamwork in advancing AI safety and reducing bias [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Lilian Weng, an Applied AI researcher at OpenAI, discusses the importance of continuous learning and collaboration in AI development. She shares her experience leading projects focused on language model safety, including efforts to detect and reduce harmful content and social biases in AI outputs. Weng emphasizes that current AI models inherit societal biases from training data and describes her team's work on mitigating these issues through evaluation pipelines and human-in-the-loop methods. She also reflects on her background in robotics and the value of persistent teamwork in overcoming complex challenges, underscoring the ongoing commitment to making AI safer and more effective.

item.title: OpenAI releases Point-E, a system generating 3D point clouds from text prompts in 1-2 minutes on a single GPU [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has developed Point-E, a system that generates 3D point clouds from complex textual prompts using a two-step diffusion model process. The method first creates a synthetic image from text and then produces a 3D point cloud conditioned on that image, enabling faster 3D model generation compared to previous approaches.

item.title: OpenAI launches text-embedding-ada-002 model, unifying five embedding models with improved performance, longer context, smaller size, and 99.8% lower price [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduced the text-embedding-ada-002 model, which replaces five separate embedding models for text search, similarity, and code search. The new model offers stronger performance, supports longer context lengths up to 8192 tokens, and produces smaller embeddings with 1536 dimensions, making it more cost-effective and efficient. The model is priced 99.8% lower than the previous Davinci model while delivering better or comparable results across various benchmarks. It simplifies the embeddings API by consolidating multiple models into one and is already being adopted by companies like Kalendar AI and Notion to improve search and recommendation capabilities. However, it may underperform on certain classification tasks compared to older models, and users are advised to evaluate performance based on their specific needs.

item.title: OpenAI engineer Christian Gibson works on optimizing backend systems for supercomputing clusters to support fast-paced AI research workflows [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Christian Gibson, an engineer on OpenAI's Supercomputing team, focuses on improving backend systems that support large-scale AI model training on billion-dollar supercomputers. His work involves identifying and resolving performance bottlenecks and hardware issues to ensure researchers can efficiently test new AI approaches without platform constraints. Gibson highlights the unique challenges of operating at OpenAI's scale, where hardware vendors encounter unprecedented issues due to the size and performance demands of the supercomputing clusters. His typical workday includes coding, debugging, and collaborating with research teams to preempt or quickly address problems, contributing to kernel and driver improvements that save significant compute time across OpenAI's infrastructure.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT, a conversational AI model trained with human feedback to engage in dialogue and handle follow-up questions [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT, a conversational AI model designed to interact through dialogue, allowing it to answer follow-up questions, admit mistakes, challenge incorrect premises, and decline inappropriate requests. The model is fine-tuned from the GPT-3.5 series using reinforcement learning from human feedback and trained on Azure AI supercomputing infrastructure. ChatGPT aims to improve user interaction by providing detailed responses and learning from feedback during its free research preview. Despite its capabilities, the model has limitations such as occasionally producing plausible but incorrect answers, sensitivity to input phrasing, verbosity, and potential biases. OpenAI encourages users to provide feedback to help address these issues and improve future versions.

item.title: OpenAI launches public beta of DALL·E API for developers to integrate image generation into apps [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has launched the public beta of the DALL·E API, enabling developers to incorporate DALL·E's image generation capabilities into their applications. The API supports creating and editing original images from natural language descriptions, with built-in moderation filters to handle content safety. Early adopters include Microsoft, which integrates DALL·E into its Designer app and Bing Image Creator, as well as startups like CALA and Mixtiles using the API for fashion design and photo art creation. The DALL·E API joins OpenAI's existing API offerings such as GPT-3 and Codex, expanding tools available for building AI-powered applications.

item.title: OpenAI studies scaling laws of reward model overoptimization in reinforcement learning from human feedback [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI researchers analyzed how optimizing against proxy reward models trained to predict human preferences can lead to overoptimization, reducing true performance in reinforcement learning. Using a synthetic setup with a fixed gold-standard reward model, they measured how optimization methods and model size affect this phenomenon, revealing distinct functional relationships and smooth scaling with reward model parameters. The study also examined the impact of dataset size, policy parameters, and KL penalty coefficients, providing empirical insights relevant to AI alignment and the design of more reliable reward models.

item.title: OpenAI removes waitlist for DALL·E beta, enabling immediate access for over 1.5 million users generating 2 million images daily [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has eliminated the waitlist for its DALL·E beta image generation tool, allowing new users to sign up and start creating images immediately. This change follows months of iterative deployment, user feedback, and improvements to safety systems that filter out inappropriate content. Since its research preview in April 2022, DALL·E has grown to over 1.5 million active users producing more than 2 million images daily, with features like Outpainting added based on artist input. OpenAI is also testing a DALL·E API for developers and businesses to build applications on the platform.

item.title: OpenAI launches Whisper, a multilingual speech recognition system trained on 680,000 hours of diverse audio data, supporting transcription and translation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced Whisper, an automatic speech recognition system trained on 680,000 hours of multilingual and multitask supervised data collected from the web. Whisper uses an encoder-decoder Transformer architecture to transcribe audio into text, identify languages, provide timestamps, and translate speech into English. The system is designed to be robust to accents, background noise, and technical language, and it supports multiple languages with improved accuracy compared to prior models. Whisper was trained on a large and diverse dataset without fine-tuning on specific benchmarks, resulting in strong zero-shot performance across various datasets and reducing errors by 50% compared to specialized models. About one-third of its training data is non-English, enabling effective speech-to-text translation. OpenAI has open-sourced the models and inference code to facilitate development of voice interfaces and further research in speech processing.

item.title: OpenAI launches Outpainting feature for DALL·E to extend images beyond original borders using natural language prompts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced Outpainting, a new feature for its DALL·E image generation model that allows users to extend images beyond their original borders by adding visual elements in the same style through natural language descriptions. This feature complements DALL·E's existing Inpainting capability and enables the creation of larger images in any aspect ratio while maintaining the original image's context, including shadows and textures. Outpainting is now available to all DALL·E users on desktop, with over one million people already using DALL·E as a creative tool. Artists have contributed to exploring the feature's capabilities by creating original extended images, demonstrating its potential for expanding creative expression.

item.title: OpenAI outlines its iterative approach to AI alignment research focusing on human feedback and AI-assisted evaluation to build safer, aligned AGI systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI is advancing its AI alignment research by improving AI systems' ability to learn from human feedback and assist humans in evaluating AI performance. Their goal is to develop sufficiently aligned AI that can help address broader alignment challenges on the path to artificial general intelligence (AGI). The approach involves training AI models using human feedback, enabling AI to assist in human evaluation, and training AI to conduct alignment research itself. The organization uses reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) as a core technique, exemplified by models like InstructGPT, which are fine-tuned to follow human intent including truthfulness and safety. While current models show improvements, they still face challenges such as occasional failures to follow instructions or produce biased responses. OpenAI emphasizes transparency in sharing alignment research and aims to refine these methods to support safer AGI development.

item.title: OpenAI launches improved Moderation endpoint for content filtering, offering free API access to developers with faster, more accurate detection of prohibited content [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced the Moderation endpoint, an enhanced content moderation tool that uses GPT-based classifiers to detect sexual, hateful, violent, or self-harm promoting content. This tool is available for free to developers using the OpenAI API to help protect applications from misuse and ensure safer AI deployment at scale. The Moderation endpoint is designed to be fast and accurate across various applications, reducing the risk of inappropriate outputs and enabling AI use in sensitive contexts like education. OpenAI also published a technical paper and evaluation dataset detailing the methodology and performance, encouraging further research in content moderation.

item.title: OpenAI develops efficient training method for autoregressive language models to perform fill-in-the-middle text prediction without harming left-to-right generation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI researchers have introduced a data transformation technique that trains autoregressive language models to infill missing text segments by moving a span from the middle of a document to its end. This method maintains the models' original left-to-right generative abilities while enhancing their infilling capabilities. The team conducted extensive experiments to optimize training parameters and released their best infilling model and benchmarks to support future research in this area.

item.title: OpenAI proposes hazard analysis framework for code synthesis large language models to identify and mitigate safety risks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has developed a hazard analysis framework aimed at uncovering technical, social, political, and economic risks associated with deploying large language models like Codex for code generation. The framework evaluates these models' ability to understand and execute complex code specifications compared to human performance, addressing alignment and misuse concerns. The analysis highlights potential limitations and safety impacts of advanced code synthesis models, emphasizing the need for careful assessment as these technologies progress. This framework supports safer deployment by systematically identifying hazards that could arise from widespread use of code-generating AI systems.

item.title: OpenAI launches DALL·E beta with free monthly credits and paid options for additional image generations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has opened beta access to DALL·E, its AI image generation tool, inviting one million users from its waitlist over the coming weeks. Users receive 50 free credits in their first month and 15 free credits monthly thereafter, with the option to purchase additional credits in increments of 115 generations for $15. The platform allows users to create, edit, and vary images using natural language prompts and grants full commercial rights to generated images, including those created during the research preview phase. The beta includes safety measures such as content filters to prevent harmful or deceptive images, restrictions on generating realistic faces of public figures, and techniques to reduce bias in image generation. OpenAI also offers subsidized access for qualifying artists and plans to gather user feedback to refine pricing and features during the beta period.

item.title: OpenAI implements new technique in DALL·E 2 to generate more diverse images of people and enhance safety measures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a system-level technique in DALL·E 2 to produce images of people that better reflect global diversity, particularly when prompts do not specify race or gender. This change has made users 12 times more likely to see diverse representations in generated images. The update is part of ongoing efforts to reduce bias and improve safety in the image generation system. During the research preview phase, OpenAI gathered user feedback on biased and sensitive images, which informed this mitigation approach. Additional safety improvements include blocking realistic face uploads, preventing likenesses of public figures, refining content filters, and enhancing monitoring systems to prevent misuse. OpenAI plans to continue refining these techniques as it expands access to DALL·E 2 to learn from real-world use and improve safety.

item.title: OpenAI says over 3,000 artists in 118 countries have integrated DALL·E 2 into creative workflows during research preview [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI reports that more than 3,000 artists across over 118 countries have incorporated DALL·E 2, its AI image generation tool, into their creative processes during the research preview phase. These early users have helped identify new applications and influenced feature development for the tool. Artists using DALL·E 2 span diverse fields including illustration, augmented reality design, writing, culinary arts, architecture, tattoo design, directing, sound design, and dance. Examples include projects for pediatric cancer patients, reinterpretations of historical art, magazine cover creation, restaurant design inspiration, and educational initiatives to make creative technology more accessible.

item.title: OpenAI applies pre-training data filtering and reweighting to DALL·E 2 to reduce graphic content, bias amplification, and image memorization risks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI implemented pre-training mitigations for DALL·E 2 by filtering and reweighting its training dataset of hundreds of millions of captioned images to reduce the generation of graphic violence and sexual content, address bias amplification, and limit memorization of training images. These measures aim to prevent the model from producing inappropriate or biased images and to encourage novel image generation. The mitigations include training in-house classifiers to remove violent and sexual images before training, using active learning and nearest neighbor search to improve classifier accuracy, and removing visually similar images to reduce memorization. OpenAI prioritized recall over precision in filtering to ensure harmful content is excluded, while continuing to study the effects of these interventions on model behavior and safety.

item.title: OpenAI trains neural network to play Minecraft using Video PreTraining on 70,000 hours of unlabeled gameplay video and fine-tuning with labeled data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI developed a neural network trained through Video PreTraining (VPT) on a large dataset of unlabeled human Minecraft gameplay videos, supplemented by a smaller labeled dataset of keypresses and mouse movements. After fine-tuning, the model can perform complex tasks such as crafting diamond tools, which typically require skilled human players over 20 minutes and 24,000 actions, using the native human interface. The training process involved creating an inverse dynamics model to predict player actions from video frames, enabling labeling of extensive online video data for behavioral cloning. The resulting foundation model can perform a variety of in-game skills including chopping trees, crafting items, swimming, hunting, and building shelters, demonstrating progress toward general-purpose agents capable of using computer interfaces.

item.title: OpenAI explores evolution through large language models to improve genetic programming and generate functional Python programs for robotic tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI's research demonstrates that large language models trained to generate code can enhance mutation operators in genetic programming by approximating human-like changes. Their experiment combined these models with MAP-Elites to produce hundreds of thousands of functional Python programs that control ambulating robots in a domain unseen during pre-training. This approach enabled bootstrapping new conditional language models capable of generating context-specific robotic walkers without prior training data, suggesting new directions for open-ended learning, deep learning, and reinforcement learning research.

item.title: OpenAI trains AI models to write critiques that help humans identify flaws in summaries, with larger models showing better self-critiquing abilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI developed AI models that generate critiques highlighting flaws in text summaries, enabling human evaluators to detect issues more frequently. Larger models demonstrated stronger self-critiquing skills, improving critique quality more than summary generation. This approach aims to assist human oversight in complex tasks by providing meaningful AI feedback. The research involved training models on topic-based summaries from various sources and showed that human evaluators assisted by AI critiques found significantly more flaws than those without assistance. Despite progress, models still struggle to fully articulate all known problems, indicating ongoing challenges in AI alignment and evaluation assistance.

item.title: OpenAI details techniques for training large neural networks using GPU parallelism methods including data, pipeline, and tensor parallelism [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI explains the challenges of training large neural networks, which require coordinating multiple GPUs to perform synchronized computations. The article outlines key parallelism techniques such as data parallelism, pipeline parallelism, tensor parallelism, and mixture-of-experts to distribute training workloads across GPUs efficiently. Data parallelism involves copying model parameters across GPUs and processing different data subsets simultaneously, while pipeline parallelism partitions model layers across GPUs to reduce memory usage per device. The article also discusses strategies to mitigate communication overhead and idle time during training, highlighting the engineering complexities involved in scaling neural network training.

item.title: Cohere, OpenAI, and AI21 Labs publish joint best practices for safe deployment of large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Cohere, OpenAI, and AI21 Labs have collaboratively developed an initial set of best practices to guide organizations in the responsible development and deployment of large language models (LLMs). These guidelines aim to mitigate risks such as misuse, bias, and unintentional harm while encouraging transparency and stakeholder collaboration. The recommendations include prohibiting harmful uses like spam and discrimination, enforcing usage policies through technical controls, and proactively addressing model limitations through evaluation and human feedback. The organizations emphasize the importance of diverse teams, public disclosure of safety lessons, and ethical treatment of labor involved in model development. They invite other providers to adopt and contribute to these evolving principles to promote safer AI deployment globally.

item.title: OpenAI shows GPT-3 can express calibrated uncertainty in natural language without using model logits [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers at OpenAI demonstrated that GPT-3 can generate both answers and corresponding confidence levels expressed in natural language, such as "90% confidence" or "high confidence," which align well with actual probabilities. This verbalized uncertainty remains moderately calibrated even under distribution shifts and reflects the model's own uncertainty rather than mimicking human examples. The team introduced the CalibratedMath suite to test this capability and found that GPT-3's ability to generalize calibration depends on pre-trained latent representations linked to epistemic uncertainty.

item.title: OpenAI Codex powers 70 applications across creativity, learning, and productivity via API since 2022 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI Codex, a natural language-to-code system based on GPT-3, is powering 70 applications across various use cases through the OpenAI API. It supports developers by converting English instructions into code in multiple languages and is the core technology behind GitHub Copilot, which suggests code in editors like Visual Studio and Visual Studio Code. Microsoft's Azure OpenAI Service offers enterprise access to Codex and other models, with applications spanning industries such as healthcare and financial services. Notable uses include Pygma, which converts Figma designs into frontend code, Replit, which helps users understand code through natural language explanations, and Warp, which enables natural language commands in the terminal to improve productivity.

item.title: OpenAI expands DALL·E 2 access with up to 1,000 new users weekly after 3 million images created and safety improvements [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has updated its DALL·E 2 research preview, reporting that early users have generated over 3 million images and helped improve safety measures including enhanced text filters and content policy enforcement. The company is now gradually onboarding up to 1,000 new users per week from its waitlist while continuing to refine its safety system and requiring adherence to content policies. OpenAI has also implemented restrictions on sharing photorealistic images with faces to address biases inherited from training data, asking users to flag problematic content. These steps aim to limit potential harm as the platform expands access and learns from real-world use.

item.title: OpenAI announces executive leadership changes including Greg Brockman as President and Mira Murati as CTO to support AI development and business strategy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has updated its executive leadership team to align with its recent progress and future goals. Greg Brockman is appointed President, focusing on AI system training and company strategy, while Mira Murati becomes Chief Technology Officer, overseeing research, product, and partnerships. Brad Lightcap is promoted to Chief Operating Officer to enhance business and commercial strategies, and Chris Clark will lead nonprofit operations and strategic initiatives. These changes aim to maintain momentum toward OpenAI's next major milestones.

item.title: OpenAI proposes hierarchical two-stage model using CLIP latents for text-conditional image generation to improve diversity and maintain photorealism [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduces a two-stage image generation model that first generates a CLIP image embedding from a text caption and then decodes an image conditioned on that embedding. This approach enhances image diversity with minimal loss in photorealism and caption similarity while enabling variations that preserve semantics and style. The model uses diffusion decoders and explores both autoregressive and diffusion priors, finding diffusion priors more efficient and higher quality. The joint CLIP embedding space also allows zero-shot language-guided image manipulations.

item.title: OpenAI analyzes Goodhart's law in optimizing proxy objectives for AI alignment using best-of-n sampling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI explores Goodhart's law, which states that when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure, in the context of optimizing AI objectives that are difficult or costly to measure. The company focuses on using proxy objectives, such as reward models trained to predict human preferences, to guide AI alignment efforts for models like GPT-3. The analysis centers on best-of-n sampling, a method where multiple samples are generated and the one scoring highest on the proxy objective is selected. This approach is mathematically tractable and competitive with reinforcement learning, allowing OpenAI to study the relationship between optimizing proxy objectives and true objectives. The post details the mathematical framework for estimating how well the true objective is optimized and how much optimization has occurred, using concepts like expectation and KL divergence.

item.title: OpenAI updates GPT-3 and Codex with edit and insert capabilities to revise and add content within existing text, enabling new use cases including code refactoring and writing [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has released new versions of GPT-3 and Codex that can edit or insert content within existing text, moving beyond their previous function of only completing text. These capabilities allow users to revise paragraphs, add contextually relevant text in the middle of content, and improve tasks such as code refactoring and documentation. The insert feature is particularly useful for software development, enabling additions to the middle of code files with awareness of surrounding code, and is being piloted in GitHub Copilot. The edits endpoint allows targeted modifications based on instructions, such as changing tone, fixing spelling, or translating code between languages. Both features are available in beta through the OpenAI API and Playground interfaces.

item.title: OpenAI outlines research agenda to assess economic impacts of code generation models including productivity, employment, and inequality [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has developed a research program to evaluate the economic effects of code generation models like Codex, focusing on their influence on productivity, labor markets, and the software industry. The agenda aims to inform policymakers, firms, and the public by studying key areas such as employment, skill development, competition, consumer prices, and economic inequality. The program invites collaboration with external researchers to measure these impacts and develop methodologies applicable to future large language models. OpenAI highlights the importance of this research for guiding deployment policy, AI system design, and public policy decisions as model capabilities advance.

item.title: OpenAI launches research initiative on economic impacts of large language models, inviting external researchers and industry partners [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has announced a call for expressions of interest to study the economic impacts of its large language models, including Codex, GPT-3, ChatGPT, and DALL-E 2. The initiative aims to understand how these AI technologies affect economic factors, labor markets, and wealth distribution to inform smarter AI development, deployment decisions, and public policy. The company seeks PhD-level researchers and industry collaborators to support this research through partnerships, API credits, and connections to AI-adopting firms. OpenAI emphasizes the importance of rigorous measurement of economic impacts to address issues like income inequality and labor market disruptions, aiming to guide policies that maximize benefits and minimize harms from AI advancements.

item.title: OpenAI shares lessons learned on language model safety and misuse from real-world deployment since 2020 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI discusses insights gained from deploying language models like GPT-3 and Codex via its API since 2020, focusing on safety challenges and misuse prevention. The company outlines its iterative deployment approach, including risk analysis, user monitoring, and policy development to reduce harms while enabling diverse applications. The article details OpenAI's strategies such as pre-training data curation, fine-tuning for instruction following, and building tools to screen harmful outputs. It acknowledges past limitations, like insufficient filtering of toxic data in early models, and emphasizes continuous improvement in safety measures and misuse detection. OpenAI highlights the complexity of responsible deployment and the need for a holistic, evolving approach to manage risks effectively.

item.title: OpenAI develops neural theorem prover for Lean that solves challenging high-school math olympiad problems including AMC12, AIME, and adapted IMO questions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has created a neural theorem prover integrated with the Lean proof assistant that learns to solve complex high-school mathematics olympiad problems. The system demonstrated improved performance on the miniF2F benchmark, achieving a new state-of-the-art by iteratively training on newly discovered proofs and tackling problems from AMC12, AIME, and adapted International Mathematical Olympiad challenges. The approach, called statement curriculum learning, involves training the model on statements of increasing difficulty without initial proofs, allowing it to progressively handle harder problems. The prover uses a language model to generate proof steps and mathematical terms, overcoming challenges such as an infinite action space and the lack of self-play in formal mathematics. This method enables the system to chain multiple non-trivial reasoning steps and produce verified formal proofs.

item.title: OpenAI launches InstructGPT models fine-tuned with human feedback to improve instruction following, truthfulness, and safety over GPT-3 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has developed InstructGPT models that better follow user instructions, produce fewer falsehoods, and generate less toxic content compared to GPT-3 by using reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). These models, trained with human demonstrations and preference rankings, are now the default on OpenAI's API. The approach improves alignment with user intentions without sacrificing performance on natural language processing benchmarks. OpenAI's research builds on prior alignment efforts and shows that fine-tuning with humans in the loop can enhance language model safety and reliability.

item.title: OpenAI launches new API endpoint for text and code embeddings to improve semantic search, clustering, and classification tasks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a new embeddings endpoint in its API that generates numerical representations of text and code to facilitate tasks such as semantic search, clustering, topic modeling, and classification. These embeddings use neural network models derived from GPT-3 and outperform previous models on benchmarks, including a 20% improvement in code search. The embeddings capture semantic similarity by mapping inputs to high-dimensional vectors, enabling efficient comparison and retrieval. OpenAI offers three families of embedding models tailored for text similarity, text search, and code search, supporting various applications like document retrieval and code relevance. The models have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance on standard evaluation suites such as SentEval and CodeSearchNet.

item.title: OpenAI releases contrastive pre-training method for text and code embeddings, achieving state-of-the-art results in semantic search and classification tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has developed a contrastive pre-training approach for generating embeddings of text and code, which improves vector representations by learning to distinguish related from unrelated pairs. This unsupervised method achieves new state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, including a 23.4% improvement on MSMARCO semantic search and a 20.8% gain in code search accuracy compared to prior models. The approach uses large-scale unsupervised data to train models that perform competitively with fine-tuned counterparts across seven classification tasks and various semantic search datasets. By applying the same technique to (text, code) pairs, OpenAI also significantly advances code embedding quality, demonstrating the method's versatility across natural language and programming domains.

item.title: OpenAI fine-tunes GPT-3 to use a text-based web browser for improved factual accuracy in answering open-ended questions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has enhanced GPT-3 by training it to operate a text-based web browser that mimics human online research, allowing the model to submit search queries, navigate web pages, and cite sources to improve the factual accuracy of its responses. This approach aims to reduce hallucinated information and make it easier for humans to evaluate and provide feedback on the model's answers. The model was fine-tuned using human demonstrations and reinforcement learning to optimize helpfulness and accuracy, with evaluations showing it performs comparably to human demonstrators on certain datasets but still faces challenges with out-of-distribution questions and unreliable sources. OpenAI highlights the importance of source citation for assessing factual accuracy and acknowledges ongoing risks and limitations, including the potential for models to selectively quote sources to appear convincing.

item.title: OpenAI launches streamlined fine-tuning for GPT-3, enabling custom models with a single command to improve accuracy and reduce costs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a simplified process for fine-tuning GPT-3 models on user-provided data, allowing developers to create custom versions tailored to specific applications with a single command. This customization improves reliability, accuracy, and efficiency across various natural language tasks, making GPT-3 more suitable for production use. The fine-tuning process supports datasets of any size and can be updated incrementally with new data, leading to significant performance gains such as reducing error rates by up to 50% and increasing accuracy from 83% to 95% in some cases. Several companies, including Keeper Tax, Viable, Sana Labs, and Elicit, have reported improvements in their applications by customizing GPT-3, with benefits ranging from better tax transaction classification to more accurate research question answering. Custom versions also reduce prompt length, lowering costs and latency. OpenAI provides documentation and API access for all customers to start fine-tuning GPT-3 models immediately.

item.title: OpenAI launches Residency program to train and hire AI researchers and engineers starting April 2022 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced the OpenAI Residency program to support and develop talent in artificial intelligence by providing a six-month, fully salaried opportunity for researchers and engineers to work on active projects. The program targets individuals without a current AI focus and aims to increase diversity and inclusion by encouraging applications from underrepresented groups and those with unconventional backgrounds. The Residency replaces previous Scholars and Fellows programs, emphasizing hands-on collaboration over curriculum-based learning. OpenAI plans to offer immigration and relocation support to global candidates and expects the program to help build a diverse pipeline of AI talent to advance its mission of creating beneficial artificial general intelligence.

item.title: OpenAI removes waitlist for API access, enabling immediate use in supported countries following safety improvements [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has eliminated the waitlist for its API, allowing developers in supported countries to sign up and start using the service immediately. This change follows advancements in safety features and content filtering that enable broader and safer access to the GPT-3 models. The company has enhanced its API with improved instruction adherence, specialized endpoints for truthful responses, and a free content filter to mitigate misuse. OpenAI continues to monitor applications for abuse and supports developers in scaling their products responsibly, while updating content guidelines to prohibit harmful or inappropriate uses such as hate speech, harassment, and adult content. These measures aim to facilitate responsible AI deployment and expand API use cases over time.

item.title: OpenAI trains a system that solves grade school math word problems with nearly double the accuracy of fine-tuned GPT-3, achieving 55% accuracy compared to 60% by children [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has developed a new AI system that solves grade school math word problems with about 55% accuracy, nearly twice as accurate as a fine-tuned GPT-3 model and close to the 60% accuracy achieved by a small group of 9-12 year olds. The system uses a verification approach, generating multiple candidate solutions and selecting the best one, which helps it recognize and correct its mistakes during multistep reasoning tasks. The model was trained and evaluated on the GSM8K dataset, which contains 8,500 diverse grade school math problems requiring multiple calculation steps. OpenAI's approach improves performance significantly over previous models by training verifiers to assess solution correctness, enabling the system to outperform much larger models and scale better with additional data. This advancement highlights progress toward AI systems capable of more reliable logical reasoning in complex domains.

item.title: OpenAI trains GPT-3 fine-tuned model to summarize entire books using human feedback and recursive task decomposition, achieving near-human summary quality [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI developed a model fine-tuned from GPT-3 that summarizes entire books by recursively summarizing smaller sections, enabling scalable human evaluation of complex AI outputs. The model achieves summary quality comparable to human-written summaries on some books and sets state-of-the-art results on the BookSum dataset. This approach addresses the challenge of evaluating long texts by breaking down tasks and empowering humans to assess summaries more efficiently, advancing research on aligning AI systems with human intentions for safer deployment.

item.title: OpenAI launches TruthfulQA benchmark to evaluate language models' tendency to replicate human falsehoods across 38 categories [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduced TruthfulQA, a benchmark with 817 questions designed to measure how language models generate truthful answers and avoid mimicking common human misconceptions. The benchmark covers diverse topics including health, law, finance, and politics, highlighting the challenge of false answers learned from training data. Testing showed that the best model answered truthfully on 58% of questions compared to 94% for humans, with larger models often being less truthful. The findings suggest that simply scaling model size may not improve truthfulness, emphasizing the need for fine-tuning beyond imitation of web text.

item.title: OpenAI appoints Helen Toner to board of directors to advance AI safety and global strategy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has appointed Helen Toner, Director of Strategy at Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology, to its board of directors. Toner brings expertise in AI policy, global AI strategy, and national security implications, supporting OpenAI's mission to ensure AI benefits all humanity. Toner oversees data-driven AI policy research at CSET and has advised policymakers on AI strategy, including analysis of AI developments in China. OpenAI leaders highlighted her understanding of AI risks and safety as critical to their efforts toward responsible AI deployment.

item.title: OpenAI launches improved Codex AI system for translating natural language into code, available via private beta API [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has released an enhanced version of its Codex AI, which converts natural language commands into working code, through a private beta API. Codex supports over a dozen programming languages and powers tools like GitHub Copilot, aiming to simplify coding by interpreting user intent and automating code generation. The system is a descendant of GPT-3, trained on natural language and billions of lines of publicly available source code, with improved memory capacity for handling Python code. OpenAI is offering Codex free during the initial beta period while working closely with developers to monitor its impact and safety.

item.title: OpenAI releases Triton 1.0, an open-source Python-like language for efficient GPU programming of neural networks without CUDA expertise [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has launched Triton 1.0, an open-source programming language designed to enable researchers without CUDA experience to write high-performance GPU code for neural networks. Triton aims to simplify GPU programming by automating complex optimizations and allowing users to achieve performance comparable to expert-tuned CUDA implementations. Triton abstracts away many GPU programming challenges such as memory coalescing, shared memory management, and instruction scheduling within streaming multiprocessors. It uses a Python-like syntax and exposes intra-instance parallelism, making it easier to write efficient kernels like FP16 matrix multiplications and fused softmax operations. OpenAI's researchers have demonstrated that Triton kernels can be up to twice as efficient as equivalent Torch implementations, and the company hopes the open-source release will foster broader community adoption and innovation in GPU programming for deep learning.

item.title: OpenAI evaluates Codex, a GPT model fine-tuned on GitHub code, showing improved Python code generation over GPT-3 and GPT-J [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduced Codex, a GPT language model fine-tuned on publicly available GitHub code, and evaluated its ability to generate Python programs from docstrings using a new benchmark called HumanEval. Codex solved 28.8% of problems on a single sample, outperforming GPT-3 and GPT-J, and achieved 70.2% success with repeated sampling. The evaluation revealed Codex's strengths and limitations, including challenges with complex docstrings and variable binding. OpenAI also discussed potential impacts of deploying advanced code generation models, addressing safety, security, and economic considerations.

item.title: OpenAI improves language model behavior by fine-tuning on a curated dataset of fewer than 100 examples targeting specific values [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI reports that fine-tuning large language models on a small, carefully curated dataset of under 100 examples can significantly improve model behavior aligned with specific social and ethical values. This approach is more effective with larger models and aims to help users tailor model outputs to their desired behavioral standards while maintaining performance on other tasks. The process involved selecting sensitive topic categories related to human wellbeing and rights, crafting a question-answer format dataset reflecting desirable behaviors, and fine-tuning GPT-3 models ranging from 125 million to 175 billion parameters. Evaluations showed statistically significant improvements in adherence to targeted values without compromising downstream task performance, suggesting a scalable method for adapting language models to diverse user values and contexts.

item.title: OpenAI announces completion of 2021 Scholars program with open-source research projects after six-month mentorship [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The 2021 OpenAI Scholars have completed a six-month mentorship program supported by OpenAI, culminating in the creation of open-source research projects. Participants worked alongside OpenAI researchers on topics including AI safety, generative modeling, and natural language processing. The program provided stipends and mentorship to nine scholars, who shared their final projects and reflected on the program's impact on their careers.

item.title: OpenAI adds former Congressman Will Hurd to board of directors to enhance AI policy and technology expertise [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has appointed former U.S. Congressman Will Hurd to its board of directors, highlighting the importance of combining public policy and technology expertise to advance its mission of developing general-purpose artificial intelligence for the benefit of all humanity. Hurd served three terms in Congress, coauthored bipartisan AI strategy legislation, and brings experience in technology policy and national security. OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman and CTO Greg Brockman emphasized Hurd's unique qualifications in AI and public policy as critical to the organization's future. Hurd expressed enthusiasm about joining OpenAI, praising its scientific advances and commitment to responsible AI development. He currently serves as managing director at Allen & Company and holds a computer science degree from Texas A&M University.

item.title: OpenAI says over 300 applications use GPT-3 API for AI-powered search, conversation, and text completion, generating 4.5 billion words daily [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI reports that more than 300 applications are leveraging its GPT-3 API to deliver advanced AI features such as search, conversation, and text completion, with the platform generating an average of 4.5 billion words per day. Tens of thousands of developers worldwide are building on this platform since its commercial launch nine months ago. These applications span various industries including productivity, education, creativity, and gaming. Examples include Viable, which uses GPT-3 to analyze customer feedback and generate insights; Fable Studio, which powers interactive storytelling characters like Lucy with natural language dialogue; and Algolia, which integrates GPT-3 for semantic search to improve answer relevance and precision. OpenAI continues to enhance the platform with new features like Answers and Classifications endpoints to support developers in building AI applications without fine-tuning.

item.title: OpenAI identifies multimodal neurons in CLIP that respond to concepts across images, text, and symbolic forms, explaining its robust visual classification [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers at OpenAI discovered neurons within the CLIP artificial neural network that activate in response to the same concept presented literally, symbolically, or conceptually. This finding sheds light on how CLIP achieves high accuracy in classifying diverse visual representations and offers insights into the model's learned associations and biases. The study draws parallels to multimodal neurons found in the human brain, such as the "Halle Berry" neuron, and reveals that CLIP's highest layers organize images semantically, enabling abstraction across various visual forms. The research also highlights CLIP's ability to recognize a wide range of high-level concepts, including emotions, animals, art styles, and famous people, through interpretable neuron activations.

item.title: OpenAI and academic researchers summarize capabilities, limitations, and societal effects of large language models including GPT-3 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers from OpenAI, Stanford, and other institutions convened in October 2020 to discuss the technical capabilities and societal impacts of large language models like GPT-3. The discussion covered the models' strengths in language tasks and their limitations such as biases and misinformation risks. The meeting also addressed broader ethical, safety, and societal considerations arising from widespread LLM deployment, highlighting challenges in education, employment, and information dissemination.

item.title: OpenAI scales Kubernetes clusters to 7,500 nodes to support large AI models and rapid research workflows [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has expanded its Kubernetes infrastructure to 7,500 nodes, enabling scalable support for large machine learning models like GPT-3, CLIP, and DALL·E, as well as facilitating fast iterative research such as studies on neural language model scaling laws. This scale is uncommon and required specific adaptations to maintain efficiency and reliability for their unique workloads, which often involve large jobs occupying entire nodes and using MPI for communication. The infrastructure changes include switching to native pod networking technologies to handle high throughput and large numbers of IP addresses, avoiding encapsulation to simplify network management, and optimizing for semi-stateful workloads that checkpoint regularly. OpenAI's setup prioritizes rapid iteration and scalability while addressing challenges unique to large-scale machine learning research clusters.

item.title: OpenAI launches CLIP neural network for zero-shot image classification using natural language supervision [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduced CLIP, a neural network that learns visual concepts from natural language paired with images, enabling it to perform zero-shot classification tasks without task-specific training. CLIP is trained on a wide variety of internet images and their associated text, allowing it to generalize across many visual classification benchmarks by predicting which text snippet matches an image. This approach addresses limitations of traditional vision models that require costly labeled datasets and struggle to adapt to new tasks, achieving competitive performance on benchmarks like ImageNet without using labeled examples.

item.title: OpenAI launches DALL·E, a 12-billion parameter neural network that generates images from text descriptions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has developed DALL·E, a neural network that creates images based on textual descriptions using a dataset of text-image pairs. The model can generate diverse and plausible images for a wide range of concepts expressed in natural language, including anthropomorphized animals, object combinations, and visual transformations. DALL·E is a transformer language model similar to GPT-3, trained to generate images and text tokens sequentially. It can control attributes, spatial relationships, and perspectives in generated images, though its accuracy decreases with more complex captions. OpenAI acknowledges potential societal impacts and plans to study issues like economic effects, bias, and ethical challenges related to generative models like DALL·E.

item.title: OpenAI announces departure of VP of Research Dario Amodei and organizational changes to integrate research, product, and safety under Mira Murati [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI announced that Dario Amodei, its VP of Research and co-leader in developing GPT-2 and GPT-3, is leaving after nearly five years to start a new research-focused project. The company expressed support for his departure and gratitude for his contributions. OpenAI is restructuring to emphasize the integration of research, product, and safety, appointing Mira Murati as senior vice president overseeing these areas. The company highlighted its ongoing commitment to developing safe and reliable general-purpose AI and plans to continue publishing research alongside product development.

item.title: OpenAI licenses GPT-3 technology to Microsoft for integration into its products and services [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has entered a multiyear licensing agreement with Microsoft, allowing the company to use GPT-3 technology in its own products and services. This deal is separate from OpenAI's API offering, which continues to provide developers access to GPT-3 and other language models for building applications. GPT-3, a general-purpose language model with 175 billion parameters, powers OpenAI's API and supports a wide range of English language tasks. Microsoft's license enables deeper integration of this technology beyond the API, expanding its use within Microsoft's ecosystem while OpenAI maintains API access for other users.

item.title: OpenAI develops GPT-f, a transformer-based language model that generates original mathematical proofs accepted into the Metamath library [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI researchers created GPT-f, an automated theorem prover using transformer-based language models to generate original mathematical terms and proofs. GPT-f successfully found new short proofs that were incorporated into the main Metamath formal mathematics library, marking the first time a deep learning system contributed accepted proofs to a formal mathematics community. The work addresses a key limitation of automated theorem provers compared to humans by leveraging generative language modeling to enhance automated reasoning. This approach demonstrates the potential for language models to assist in formal proof generation and mathematical discovery.

item.title: OpenAI applies reinforcement learning from human feedback to improve language model summarization, outperforming larger supervised models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has used reinforcement learning guided by human feedback to train language models that generate higher-quality summaries than models trained solely with supervised learning, even outperforming models ten times larger. The approach was tested on Reddit TL;DR data and transferred effectively to summarize CNN/DailyMail news articles without additional fine-tuning. This method aims to better align AI outputs with human preferences, addressing issues like factual inaccuracies and bias in language model generation. The models trained with human feedback showed significant improvements in summary quality as judged by human evaluators, with some preferred over original human-written summaries. This work demonstrates the potential of human feedback to enhance AI alignment and performance across diverse text summarization tasks.

item.title: OpenAI Scholars 2020 present final projects after five months of research in virtual Demo Day [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The third cohort of OpenAI Scholars showcased their final projects during a virtual Demo Day, presenting research conducted over five months. Projects included analyzing GPT-2's grammar representation, evaluating model interpretability on Coinrun, and predicting epileptic seizures from brain recordings. The OpenAI Scholars program supports individuals from underrepresented groups with stipends and mentorship to study deep learning and develop open-source projects. Microsoft provided Azure compute credits, and further details about the next class will be announced in the fall.

item.title: OpenAI, AIcrowd, Carnegie Mellon, and DeepMind co-organize Procgen and MineRL competitions at NeurIPS 2020 to advance reinforcement learning research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI is partnering with AIcrowd, Carnegie Mellon University, and DeepMind to co-host two competitions at NeurIPS 2020 focused on the Procgen Benchmark and MineRL environments, which are used internally for reinforcement learning research. The Procgen Competition challenges participants to improve sample efficiency and generalization across 16 public and 4 secret procedurally generated environments, while the MineRL Competition aims to develop algorithms that leverage human demonstrations to reduce sample complexity in Minecraft tasks. The Procgen environments require agents to generalize to new situations, providing a robust test for reinforcement learning methods, and are designed to be computationally accessible. The MineRL Competition restricts participants to 8 million simulator samples and 4 days of training on a single GPU to obtain a diamond in Minecraft, using a large dataset of human demonstrations to encourage sample-efficient learning. The competitions include strict evaluation protocols to ensure fairness and to prevent overfitting or hand-engineered solutions, with the goal of pushing the state of the art in reinforcement learning efficiency and generalization.

item.title: OpenAI demonstrates that a large transformer model trained on pixel sequences can generate coherent images and achieve competitive unsupervised classification accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers at OpenAI have shown that a transformer model similar to those used in language processing can be trained on sequences of pixels to generate coherent image completions and samples. This model, called Image GPT, also produces features that perform competitively with leading convolutional neural networks in unsupervised image classification tasks. The study highlights a correlation between the quality of generated images and classification accuracy, suggesting that generative sequence modeling can serve as a general-purpose unsupervised learning algorithm. By applying the same transformer architecture used in GPT-2 for language to images, the researchers achieved state-of-the-art results on several image classification benchmarks without relying on domain-specific architectural designs.

item.title: OpenAI launches API for accessing its GPT-3 family AI models with text completion capabilities in private beta [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has released an API that provides developers with access to its general-purpose AI models, including those from the GPT-3 family, allowing text input and output for a wide range of English language tasks. The API is currently in private beta and supports customization through training on user-provided datasets or human feedback. The API aims to make powerful AI technology more accessible to smaller businesses and researchers while enabling OpenAI to monitor and mitigate misuse, such as harassment or disinformation. OpenAI plans to continuously upgrade the API and share safety research to promote responsible AI deployment and development.

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-3, a 175-billion-parameter language model demonstrating strong few-shot learning across diverse NLP tasks without fine-tuning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduced GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, which achieves competitive performance on various natural language processing tasks using few-shot learning without task-specific fine-tuning. GPT-3 can handle translation, question-answering, cloze tasks, and on-the-fly reasoning such as arithmetic and word usage by interacting through text prompts alone. The model surpasses previous approaches by scaling up parameters and training on a large corpus, enabling it to generalize from minimal examples. However, GPT-3 still faces challenges on certain datasets and methodological issues related to training data. It can also generate news articles that human evaluators find difficult to distinguish from human-written content, raising broader societal considerations.

item.title: OpenAI analysis shows compute needed to train neural nets for ImageNet classification halved every 16 months since 2012, with 44x less compute needed now than then [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI released an analysis revealing that since 2012, the computational resources required to train neural networks to AlexNet-level performance on ImageNet classification have decreased by half every 16 months. This improvement results in 44 times less compute needed today compared to 2012, surpassing the 11-fold efficiency gain predicted by Moore's Law over the same period. The findings suggest that algorithmic advancements have contributed more to AI efficiency gains than hardware improvements for tasks with significant recent investment. The analysis also notes similar efficiency improvements in other AI tasks such as translation, Go, and Dota 2, with examples including the Transformer model achieving 61 times less training compute than previous methods within three years. OpenAI highlights that these algorithmic efficiency gains enable faster experimentation and accelerate future AI research, analogous to having more computational power. However, the report acknowledges limitations due to the small number of data points and the uncertainty about how broadly these trends apply across AI domains.

item.title: OpenAI launches Jukebox, a neural network generating raw audio music and singing across genres with released model weights and code [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced Jukebox, a neural network that generates music and rudimentary singing as raw audio in various genres and artist styles. The company has released the model weights, code, and an interactive tool to explore generated music samples. Jukebox uses a hierarchical VQ-VAE autoencoder to compress audio into discrete codes and transformer-based priors to generate music in this compressed space, enabling the creation of high-level musical structures and local details. This approach addresses challenges in modeling long-range dependencies and audio fidelity in raw audio music generation.

item.title: OpenAI and 29 organizations propose 10 mechanisms to improve verifiability of AI system claims for safety, fairness, and privacy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A collaborative report by 58 authors from 30 organizations, including OpenAI and major research centers, outlines ten mechanisms to enhance the verifiability of claims about AI systems. These mechanisms aim to help developers provide evidence that AI technologies are safe, secure, fair, and privacy-preserving, while enabling users, policymakers, and civil society to evaluate AI development practices. The report highlights institutional, software, and hardware approaches such as third-party auditing, red teaming exercises, bias and safety bounties, sharing AI incident information, audit trails, interpretability research, privacy-preserving machine learning tools, secure hardware development, precise compute measurement, and increased compute support for academia. The authors emphasize the importance of these mechanisms to improve transparency and trustworthiness in AI development and encourage further collaboration on these issues.

item.title: OpenAI launches Microscope tool to visualize neurons and layers in eight common vision models for interpretability research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced Microscope, a tool that provides visualizations of every significant layer and neuron in eight widely studied vision models to facilitate analysis of feature formation in neural networks. The tool aims to accelerate research by enabling quick exploration and sharing of neuron interactions, supporting collaboration across institutions. Microscope builds on open-source visualization techniques and makes neurons linkable to reduce confusion and improve scrutiny of research claims. It focuses on a small set of models to provide detailed insights and plans to expand to more models and techniques, supporting projects like the Circuits collaboration that reverse engineer neural networks by analyzing individual neurons and their connections.

item.title: OpenAI standardizes its deep learning framework on PyTorch to improve research productivity and GPU performance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has decided to standardize its deep learning framework on PyTorch to streamline development and accelerate research iteration times, particularly on GPUs. This move aims to enhance collaboration within its teams and leverage the growing PyTorch community, including partners like Facebook and Microsoft. OpenAI has also released a PyTorch-enabled version of its educational resource Spinning Up in Deep RL and plans to open-source PyTorch bindings for its optimized blocksparse kernels in the coming months.

item.title: OpenAI publishes empirical scaling laws for neural language model performance across model size, dataset size, and compute, revealing power-law relationships and optimal training strategies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI researchers studied how neural language model performance, measured by cross-entropy loss, scales with model size, dataset size, and compute used for training. They found power-law relationships spanning over seven orders of magnitude and showed that architectural details like network width or depth have minimal impact within a broad range. The study also identified optimal compute allocation strategies, indicating that training very large models on modest data and stopping before full convergence is most compute-efficient.

item.title: OpenAI trains OpenAI Five with large-scale deep reinforcement learning to defeat Dota 2 world champions after 10 months of self-play [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
